# Extended Session Manager

This is maintained official functionality in `official/extended-session-manager`.
The stable ID `example.self-service-session-manager` is preserved for updates;
new releases use the official signer through an exact-ID trust grant. Historical
demo packages retain their original signatures. Installing a newly signed release
requires the successor public key and exact-ID policy described in
[host issue #7](https://github.com/obsoletelabs/unnamed_tracking_app_2/issues/7).

The 2.x series ports application [PR #248](https://github.com/Rosefall-a/unnamed_tracking_app/pull/248), inspected at head `5bf43f22bd4991999cd278c5b201817aae439e85`. Current branch previews use Plugin API 1.1. The stable ID remains `example.self-service-session-manager`. This replaces the minimized metadata/Refresh example.

## Experience and source parity

The primary experience is **Account → Sessions** (`/settings?area=account&section=sessions`) and administrator-only **Administration → Session Manager** (`/settings?area=administration&section=admin-sessions`). The host now supplies basic pages showing state, IP, browser details and timestamps. This plugin replaces only those two sections with its extended GeoIP, network, anomaly and map interface, using independently approved page-scoped permissions. It registers no duplicate settings entries and retains its stable plugin ID. Controls use native palette and shape tokens; no host code selects this plugin by ID.

Disabling the plugin or declining either replacement permission leaves that built-in page available. The **Advanced sessions** switch at the top of either page selects the extended or built-in view; turning it off opens the basic page with `basic=1`. Native and sandbox plugin-owned page URLs remain available. The companion host change adding `sessions` and `admin-sessions` replacement targets is merged: earlier hosts do not understand the new capabilities. Existing installations must review and grant the new replacement permissions during update.

Native cards, administration rows and selected map markers summarize browser and operating system. The full user agent is available in an expandable detail so diagnostic information remains accessible without filling every row. This formatting stays inside the plugin; it does not import host frontend code.

The 2.3.1 preview bounds native controls to the host panel. User selectors use
the shared field style, long values wrap or stay within their control, and
expanded GeoIP uploads fit narrow screens. The wide administration table keeps
its own horizontal scroller; it does not widen the surrounding settings page.

| PR #248 behavior | Current native plugin |
| --- | --- |
| Current session; active/expired/revoked records | Reproduced with backend state filtering |
| IP, user agent, country/region/city, timestamps | Reproduced, including creation, activity, expiry, revocation |
| Network type/label, ASN/network number, organization | Reproduced with the source credential-free serializer |
| Session search and admin user filters | Reproduced; country/anomaly filters also expose source metadata |
| GIS map, pan/zoom, clustered selectable pins, admin user colors | Reproduced for loaded pages when City GeoIP is usable |
| Own one/all; admin one/user/server revocation | Reproduced with separate destructive grants and explicit confirmation |
| Admin compact table, City/Country/Network MMDB status/uploads | Reproduced with scoped grants, confirmation, and existing host validation |
| Geographic anomaly and provider notifications | Source session metadata and core notification coordinator reused |

The current account session has no individual revoke button, matching the source. Revoke all includes it and returns the browser to sign-in. Bulk actions affect all unrevoked records in scope, including expired ones, regardless of displayed filters, matching the source SQL. API keys are separate and are not revoked.

Anomalies show the reason and previous location. Shared password/OIDC session creation queues `session_anomaly` notifications through the existing core coordinator, deduplication, provider registry, delivery state, and preferences. This plugin does not resend or invent alerts; notification providers/preferences stay in their normal host Settings surfaces.

The map requests visible OpenStreetMap tiles with browser caching, visible attribution, and an origin-only referrer following the [tile usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/). OSM receives the viewing browser's IP, application origin, and tile coordinates. Session identifiers, usernames, IP metadata, and user agents are never sent in tile requests. Locations are approximate; private/local addresses are not plotted.

## Permission review: intentionally high risk

| Permission | Why requested | Risk / destructive behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions.read` | Rich records owned by the caller | Sensitive device, IP, approximate location, and network metadata; never tokens/hashes |
| `sessions.revoke` | Own single/bulk revocation | **Destructive:** signs out browsers, including the current browser during bulk revocation |
| `sessions.admin.read` | Cross-user admin records | **High:** sensitive metadata across users; host admin role independently required |
| `sessions.admin.revoke` | Admin single/user/server revocation | **Destructive, High:** can sign out every browser; admin required |
| `sessions.geoip.read` | Database availability | Admin-only status without filesystem paths |
| `sessions.geoip.configure` | Replace optional MMDB databases | **Destructive, High:** changes shared enrichment data; admin and confirmation required |
| `frontend.page.replace.sessions` | Enhance the built-in account Sessions section | **High:** replaces only this page; independent of session read/revoke grants |
| `frontend.page.replace.admin-sessions` | Enhance the built-in administrator Session Manager section | **High:** replaces only this page; the host still requires administrator access |
| `frontend.native` | Native cards, table, map, file controls | **Critical:** reviewed code executes in the host browser realm, with DOM/browser authority; scoped backend grants remain enforced |
| `backend.routes.plugin` | Optional namespaced JSON handlers | Host authentication, admin policies, lifecycle, limits, and installation grants |

No `api.full`, `backend.routes.host`, arbitrary filesystem/network, broad user-read, or notification-send permission is requested. Read and revoke grants are independent. Declining a grant denies its operation; no broader fallback API is used. Without `frontend.native`, the legacy plugin-owned account page supplies a sandboxed own-session fallback with metadata and confirmed revocation. Full map/admin/configuration parity requires the reviewed native grant.

## Backend security and revocation

All destructive actions declare host-owned confirmation text. Both UI modes ask for confirmation; the backend action endpoint requires strict boolean `confirmed: true` before dispatch. The plugin and gateway also require explicit confirmation. JSON route clients must expressly confirm. Confirmation prevents accidents; it does not replace authorization.

The host authenticates the caller, checks live installation grants and health, and creates current-session context from the authenticated cookie. Caller-supplied `_plugin_context` is overwritten. The domain constrains self-service SQL to the caller and independently checks active admin status for cross-user operations. Knowing a foreign UUID cannot change ownership. Malformed UUIDs are rejected. Disabled/unhealthy plugins cannot dispatch actions, routes, or gateway methods. Plugin Python imports only the standard library and public SDK, and receives no cookies, tokens, hashes, ORM objects, or database connections.

Revocation sets `revoked_at`, preserving audit metadata. Subsequent cookie authentication fails immediately. A generic host auth refresh returns remotely revoked browsers to login; current-browser bulk revocation navigates immediately.

Optional routes relative to `/api/plugins/example.self-service-session-manager/`:

| Method/path | Grant | Caller |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET `sessions` | `sessions.read` | Owner |
| DELETE `sessions/{session_id}` / `sessions` | `sessions.revoke` | Owner |
| GET `admin/sessions` | `sessions.admin.read` | Administrator |
| DELETE `admin/sessions/{session_id}` / `admin/users/{user_id}/sessions` / `admin/sessions` | `sessions.admin.revoke` | Administrator |

DELETE bodies require `{ "confirmed": true }`. Lists accept `q`, `state`, `country`, `anomaly=true|false`, `limit` (up to 200), `cursor`, and admin-only `user_id`.

MMDB upload uses the generic host capability endpoint `POST /api/plugins/<plugin-id>/capabilities/sessions/geoip?kind=city|country|network&confirmed=true` with multipart `file`. The host validates and atomically replaces the database. Reads are bounded to 256 MiB; proxy limits can be lower. There is no automatic database download, license acquisition, or arbitrary server filesystem access.

## Platform stages 1–4 demonstrated

1. Versioned contracts, risk rationales, installation identity, ownership, separate read/write grants.
2. Normal package inspection, development trust consent, update permission review, health/lifecycle gating; the entrypoint stays alive under the supervisor.
3. Native Settings, admin visibility, host Vue integration/cleanup, host action confirmation, sandbox fallback.
4. Namespaced backend routes with authenticated/admin policies, normalized request envelopes, scoped gateway methods.

## Remaining differences from PR #248

- Lists, map pins, and the admin user selector reflect loaded cursor pages rather than one unbounded response. **Load more** exposes the remainder; search can find users beyond loaded pages.
- GeoIP configuration does not disclose host filesystem paths.
- Every single-session destructive action is confirmed; the source account's individual revoke button was immediate.
- Native integration requires reviewing Critical browser authority plus narrow domain grants. The sandbox fallback lacks map/admin/configuration UI.
- Historical sessions without metadata cannot be retroactively enriched. New sessions use the shared source metadata/anomaly path.
- External map tiles, optional MMDB availability, and configured notification delivery remain deployment dependencies, as in the source.

No source user/admin workflow is omitted from the full native experience.

## Build and verification

Requires a Plugin API/SDK 1.1 host, currently the coordinated `feat/ui-ux-redevelopment` branch. A 1.0 host cannot run this new package; its limited legacy support applies to older packages only. Capability version 1 retains its ownership scopes with additive DTO fields/new operations. Strict destructive confirmation is an intentional security tightening; older clients must send confirmation.

```sh
pytest
node --test tests/session_manager_ui.test.mjs
node tools/capture_sessions.mjs /path/to/host /path/to/evidence http://127.0.0.1:8000 /path/to/temporary-admin-cookies.json
python tools/build_packages.py
python tools/verify_packages.py dist/*.utp
python tools/validate_packages.py dist/*.utp
```

Plugin tests exercise permissions, filters, identifier validation, confirmations, routing, packaging, actual UI controller pagination/cancellation/sign-out/errors/cleanup, and map math. Host HTTP tests execute real SQL/grants for cross-user reads/writes, unauthorized revocation, strict confirmation, disabled plugins, malformed IDs, admin checks, pagination, revoked-cookie rejection, GeoIP uploads, and password metadata/anomaly creation. Existing CI checks remain, with Node UI tests added.

The browser verifier requires an installed, running native package on a disposable local host. It creates its own temporary members, exercises owner and administrator filters/confirmed revocation, verifies foreign-session denial and sign-out without refresh, and captures 320/390/1440/1920-pixel light/dark layouts. It never revokes the administrator's session or unrelated users' sessions; its fixtures are removed afterwards. The optional `SESSION_PACKAGE_SHA256` records the exact tested archive.

Local packages are **unsigned**, requiring normal untrusted-package consent. Release CI supplies its configured reviewed signing identity. Historical packages and signing identities are preserved.

The latest authenticated local-host check uses the current unsigned working-tree
preview at 320, 390, 1440 and 1920 pixels. Owner/admin filters, cancellation,
selected-user revocation, foreign-session denial and sign-out without a refresh
pass. Its [report](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-native-conformance.json)
identifies the tested archive and records the actual loaded native UI.

![Authenticated account sessions on a phone](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-owner-loaded-390-dark.png)

![Authenticated administrator session filters](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-admin-loaded-1440-light.png)

![Native admin component with fixture data](../../docs/assets/screenshots/session-manager-admin.png)

Screenshot uses the actual native module with disposable fixture data in a local Vue harness, not a deployed authenticated host.

Native cards, administration rows and selected map markers summarize browser and operating system. The full user agent is available in an expandable detail so diagnostic information remains accessible without filling every row. This formatting stays inside the plugin; it does not import host frontend code.

The 2.3.1 preview bounds native controls to the host panel. User selectors use
the shared field style, long values wrap or stay within their control, and
expanded GeoIP uploads fit narrow screens. The wide administration table keeps
its own horizontal scroller; it does not widen the surrounding settings page.

| PR #248 behavior | Current native plugin |
| --- | --- |
| Current session; active/expired/revoked records | Reproduced with backend state filtering |
| IP, user agent, country/region/city, timestamps | Reproduced, including creation, activity, expiry, revocation |
| Network type/label, ASN/network number, organization | Reproduced with the source credential-free serializer |
| Session search and admin user filters | Reproduced; country/anomaly filters also expose source metadata |
| GIS map, pan/zoom, clustered selectable pins, admin user colors | Reproduced for loaded pages when City GeoIP is usable |
| Own one/all; admin one/user/server revocation | Reproduced with separate destructive grants and explicit confirmation |
| Admin compact table, City/Country/Network MMDB status/uploads | Reproduced with scoped grants, confirmation, and existing host validation |
| Geographic anomaly and provider notifications | Source session metadata and core notification coordinator reused |

The current account session has no individual revoke button, matching the source. Revoke all includes it and returns the browser to sign-in. Bulk actions affect all unrevoked records in scope, including expired ones, regardless of displayed filters, matching the source SQL. API keys are separate and are not revoked.

Anomalies show the reason and previous location. Shared password/OIDC session creation queues `session_anomaly` notifications through the existing core coordinator, deduplication, provider registry, delivery state, and preferences. This plugin does not resend or invent alerts; notification providers/preferences stay in their normal host Settings surfaces.

The map requests visible OpenStreetMap tiles with browser caching, visible attribution, and an origin-only referrer following the [tile usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/). OSM receives the viewing browser's IP, application origin, and tile coordinates. Session identifiers, usernames, IP metadata, and user agents are never sent in tile requests. Locations are approximate; private/local addresses are not plotted.

## Permission review: intentionally high risk

| Permission | Why requested | Risk / destructive behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions.read` | Rich records owned by the caller | Sensitive device, IP, approximate location, and network metadata; never tokens/hashes |
| `sessions.revoke` | Own single/bulk revocation | **Destructive:** signs out browsers, including the current browser during bulk revocation |
| `sessions.admin.read` | Cross-user admin records | **High:** sensitive metadata across users; host admin role independently required |
| `sessions.admin.revoke` | Admin single/user/server revocation | **Destructive, High:** can sign out every browser; admin required |
| `sessions.geoip.read` | Database availability | Admin-only status without filesystem paths |
| `sessions.geoip.configure` | Replace optional MMDB databases | **Destructive, High:** changes shared enrichment data; admin and confirmation required |
| `frontend.page.replace.sessions` | Enhance the built-in account Sessions section | **High:** replaces only this page; independent of session read/revoke grants |
| `frontend.page.replace.admin-sessions` | Enhance the built-in administrator Session Manager section | **High:** replaces only this page; the host still requires administrator access |
| `frontend.native` | Native cards, table, map, file controls | **Critical:** reviewed code executes in the host browser realm, with DOM/browser authority; scoped backend grants remain enforced |
| `backend.routes.plugin` | Optional namespaced JSON handlers | Host authentication, admin policies, lifecycle, limits, and installation grants |

No `api.full`, `backend.routes.host`, arbitrary filesystem/network, broad user-read, or notification-send permission is requested. Read and revoke grants are independent. Declining a grant denies its operation; no broader fallback API is used. Without `frontend.native`, the legacy plugin-owned account page supplies a sandboxed own-session fallback with metadata and confirmed revocation. Full map/admin/configuration parity requires the reviewed native grant.

## Backend security and revocation

All destructive actions declare host-owned confirmation text. Both UI modes ask for confirmation; the backend action endpoint requires strict boolean `confirmed: true` before dispatch. The plugin and gateway also require explicit confirmation. JSON route clients must expressly confirm. Confirmation prevents accidents; it does not replace authorization.

The host authenticates the caller, checks live installation grants and health, and creates current-session context from the authenticated cookie. Caller-supplied `_plugin_context` is overwritten. The domain constrains self-service SQL to the caller and independently checks active admin status for cross-user operations. Knowing a foreign UUID cannot change ownership. Malformed UUIDs are rejected. Disabled/unhealthy plugins cannot dispatch actions, routes, or gateway methods. Plugin Python imports only the standard library and public SDK, and receives no cookies, tokens, hashes, ORM objects, or database connections.

Revocation sets `revoked_at`, preserving audit metadata. Subsequent cookie authentication fails immediately. A generic host auth refresh returns remotely revoked browsers to login; current-browser bulk revocation navigates immediately.

Optional routes relative to `/api/plugins/example.self-service-session-manager/`:

| Method/path | Grant | Caller |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET `sessions` | `sessions.read` | Owner |
| DELETE `sessions/{session_id}` / `sessions` | `sessions.revoke` | Owner |
| GET `admin/sessions` | `sessions.admin.read` | Administrator |
| DELETE `admin/sessions/{session_id}` / `admin/users/{user_id}/sessions` / `admin/sessions` | `sessions.admin.revoke` | Administrator |

DELETE bodies require `{ "confirmed": true }`. Lists accept `q`, `state`, `country`, `anomaly=true|false`, `limit` (up to 200), `cursor`, and admin-only `user_id`.

MMDB upload uses the generic host capability endpoint `POST /api/plugins/<plugin-id>/capabilities/sessions/geoip?kind=city|country|network&confirmed=true` with multipart `file`. The host validates and atomically replaces the database. Reads are bounded to 256 MiB; proxy limits can be lower. There is no automatic database download, license acquisition, or arbitrary server filesystem access.

## Platform stages 1–4 demonstrated

1. Versioned contracts, risk rationales, installation identity, ownership, separate read/write grants.
2. Normal package inspection, development trust consent, update permission review, health/lifecycle gating; the entrypoint stays alive under the supervisor.
3. Native Settings, admin visibility, host Vue integration/cleanup, host action confirmation, sandbox fallback.
4. Namespaced backend routes with authenticated/admin policies, normalized request envelopes, scoped gateway methods.

## Remaining differences from PR #248

- Lists, map pins, and the admin user selector reflect loaded cursor pages rather than one unbounded response. **Load more** exposes the remainder; search can find users beyond loaded pages.
- GeoIP configuration does not disclose host filesystem paths.
- Every single-session destructive action is confirmed; the source account's individual revoke button was immediate.
- Native integration requires reviewing Critical browser authority plus narrow domain grants. The sandbox fallback lacks map/admin/configuration UI.
- Historical sessions without metadata cannot be retroactively enriched. New sessions use the shared source metadata/anomaly path.
- External map tiles, optional MMDB availability, and configured notification delivery remain deployment dependencies, as in the source.

No source user/admin workflow is omitted from the full native experience.

## Build and verification

Requires a Plugin API/SDK 1.1 host, currently the coordinated `feat/ui-ux-redevelopment` branch. A 1.0 host cannot run this new package; its limited legacy support applies to older packages only. Capability version 1 retains its ownership scopes with additive DTO fields/new operations. Strict destructive confirmation is an intentional security tightening; older clients must send confirmation.

```sh
pytest
node --test tests/session_manager_ui.test.mjs
node tools/capture_sessions.mjs /path/to/host /path/to/evidence http://127.0.0.1:8000 /path/to/temporary-admin-cookies.json
python tools/build_packages.py
python tools/verify_packages.py dist/*.utp
python tools/validate_packages.py dist/*.utp
```

Plugin tests exercise permissions, filters, identifier validation, confirmations, routing, packaging, actual UI controller pagination/cancellation/sign-out/errors/cleanup, and map math. Host HTTP tests execute real SQL/grants for cross-user reads/writes, unauthorized revocation, strict confirmation, disabled plugins, malformed IDs, admin checks, pagination, revoked-cookie rejection, GeoIP uploads, and password metadata/anomaly creation. Existing CI checks remain, with Node UI tests added.

The browser verifier requires an installed, running native package on a disposable local host. It creates its own temporary members, exercises owner and administrator filters/confirmed revocation, verifies foreign-session denial and sign-out without refresh, and captures 320/390/1440/1920-pixel light/dark layouts. It never revokes the administrator's session or unrelated users' sessions; its fixtures are removed afterwards. The optional `SESSION_PACKAGE_SHA256` records the exact tested archive.

Local packages are **unsigned**, requiring normal untrusted-package consent. Release CI supplies its configured reviewed signing identity. Historical packages and signing identities are preserved.

The latest authenticated local-host check uses the current unsigned working-tree
preview at 320, 390, 1440 and 1920 pixels. Owner/admin filters, cancellation,
selected-user revocation, foreign-session denial and sign-out without a refresh
pass. Its [report](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-native-conformance.json)
identifies the tested archive and records the actual loaded native UI.

![Authenticated account sessions on a phone](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-owner-loaded-390-dark.png)

![Authenticated administrator session filters](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-admin-loaded-1440-light.png)

![Native admin component with fixture data](../../docs/assets/screenshots/session-manager-admin.png)

Screenshot uses the actual native module with disposable fixture data in a local Vue harness, not a deployed authenticated host.

Declining a grant denies its operation; no broader fallback API is used. Without `frontend.native`, the legacy plugin-owned account page supplies a sandboxed own-session fallback with metadata and confirmed revocation. Full map/admin/configuration parity requires the reviewed native grant.

## Backend security and revocation

All destructive actions declare host-owned confirmation text. Both UI modes ask for confirmation; the backend action endpoint requires strict boolean `confirmed: true` before dispatch. The plugin and gateway also require explicit confirmation. JSON route clients must expressly confirm. Confirmation prevents accidents; it does not replace authorization.

The host authenticates the caller, checks live installation grants and health, and creates current-session context from the authenticated cookie. Caller-supplied `_plugin_context` is overwritten. The domain constrains self-service SQL to the caller and independently checks active admin status for cross-user operations. Knowing a foreign UUID cannot change ownership. Malformed UUIDs are rejected. Disabled/unhealthy plugins cannot dispatch actions, routes, or gateway methods. Plugin Python imports only the standard library and public SDK, and receives no cookies, tokens, hashes, ORM objects, or database connections.

Revocation sets `revoked_at`, preserving audit metadata. Subsequent cookie authentication fails immediately. A generic host auth refresh returns remotely revoked browsers to login; current-browser bulk revocation navigates immediately.

| Method/path | Grant | Caller |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET `sessions` | `sessions.read` | Owner |

| GET `admin/sessions` | `sessions.admin.read` | Administrator |

DELETE bodies require `{ "confirmed": true }`. Lists accept `q`, `state`, `country`, `anomaly=true|false`, `limit` (up to 200), `cursor`, and admin-only `user_id`.

MMDB upload uses the generic host capability endpoint `POST /api/plugins/<plugin-id>/capabilities/sessions/geoip?kind=city|country|network&confirmed=true` with multipart `file`. 2. Normal package inspection, development trust consent, update permission review, health/lifecycle gating; the entrypoint stays alive under the supervisor.
3. Native Settings, admin visibility, host Vue integration/cleanup, host action confirmation, sandbox fallback.

- GeoIP configuration does not disclose host filesystem paths.
- Every single-session destructive action is confirmed; the source account's individual revoke button was immediate.
- Native integration requires reviewing Critical browser authority plus narrow domain grants. The sandbox fallback lacks map/admin/configuration UI.
- Historical sessions without metadata cannot be retroactively enriched. New sessions use the shared source metadata/anomaly path.

No source user/admin workflow is omitted from the full native experience.

node tools/capture_sessions.mjs /path/to/host /path/to/evidence http://127.0.0.1:8000 /path/to/temporary-admin-cookies.json

python tools/verify_packages.py dist/*.utp

1. Versioned contracts, risk rationales, installation identity, ownership, separate read/write grants.
2. Normal package inspection, development trust consent, update permission review, health/lifecycle gating; the entrypoint stays alive under the supervisor.
3. Native Settings, admin visibility, host Vue integration/cleanup, host action confirmation, sandbox fallback.
4. Namespaced backend routes with authenticated/admin policies, normalized request envelopes, scoped gateway methods.

## Remaining differences from PR #248

- Lists, map pins, and the admin user selector reflect loaded cursor pages rather than one unbounded response. **Load more** exposes the remainder; search can find users beyond loaded pages.
- GeoIP configuration does not disclose host filesystem paths.
- Every single-session destructive action is confirmed; the source account's individual revoke button was immediate.
- Native integration requires reviewing Critical browser authority plus narrow domain grants. The sandbox fallback lacks map/admin/configuration UI.
- Historical sessions without metadata cannot be retroactively enriched. New sessions use the shared source metadata/anomaly path.
- External map tiles, optional MMDB availability, and configured notification delivery remain deployment dependencies, as in the source.

No source user/admin workflow is omitted from the full native experience.

## Build and verification

Requires a Plugin API/SDK 1.1 host, currently the coordinated `feat/ui-ux-redevelopment` branch. A 1.0 host cannot run this new package; its limited legacy support applies to older packages only. Capability version 1 retains its ownership scopes with additive DTO fields/new operations. Strict destructive confirmation is an intentional security tightening; older clients must send confirmation.

```sh
pytest
node --test tests/session_manager_ui.test.mjs
node tools/capture_sessions.mjs /path/to/host /path/to/evidence http://127.0.0.1:8000 /path/to/temporary-admin-cookies.json
python tools/build_packages.py
python tools/verify_packages.py dist/*.utp
python tools/validate_packages.py dist/*.utp
```

Plugin tests exercise permissions, filters, identifier validation, confirmations, routing, packaging, actual UI controller pagination/cancellation/sign-out/errors/cleanup, and map math. Host HTTP tests execute real SQL/grants for cross-user reads/writes, unauthorized revocation, strict confirmation, disabled plugins, malformed IDs, admin checks, pagination, revoked-cookie rejection, GeoIP uploads, and password metadata/anomaly creation. Existing CI checks remain, with Node UI tests added.

The browser verifier requires an installed, running native package on a disposable local host. It creates its own temporary members, exercises owner and administrator filters/confirmed revocation, verifies foreign-session denial and sign-out without refresh, and captures 320/390/1440/1920-pixel light/dark layouts. It never revokes the administrator's session or unrelated users' sessions; its fixtures are removed afterwards. The optional `SESSION_PACKAGE_SHA256` records the exact tested archive.

Local packages are **unsigned**, requiring normal untrusted-package consent. Release CI supplies its configured reviewed signing identity. Historical packages and signing identities are preserved.

The latest authenticated local-host check uses the current unsigned working-tree
preview at 320, 390, 1440 and 1920 pixels. Owner/admin filters, cancellation,
selected-user revocation, foreign-session denial and sign-out without a refresh
pass. Its [report](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-native-conformance.json)
identifies the tested archive and records the actual loaded native UI.

![Authenticated account sessions on a phone](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-owner-loaded-390-dark.png)

![Authenticated administrator session filters](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-admin-loaded-1440-light.png)

![Native admin component with fixture data](../../wiki/docs/assets/screenshots/session-manager-admin.png)

Screenshot uses the actual native module with disposable fixture data in a local Vue harness, not a deployed authenticated host.

Enhance the built-in account and administrator session pages through separately approved page replacements, preserving GeoIP location, network and anomaly data, the map, database uploads and confirmed revocation. Summarize browser and operating system, with the full user agent available on demand.

# UI and API Example

A small Plugin API v1 reference with a real declarative page, a `display_mode`
settings section and a **Read library** action returning up to 50 current-user
games. It requests `games.read`, `plugin.settings` and `frontend.navigation.main`.
It also requests `tasks.background` for a **Library summary** job in Administration
→ Tasks. The schedule starts off, supports an interval and Run now, and uses the
plugin's existing background administrator identity. Its handler returns only a
bounded public summary; it does not read every user's library or opt anyone into
personal background subscriptions. Withdraw either background or library access
to pause the job. Updates and ordinary reinstall retain its schedule.
The host owns permission classification and supplies authenticated gateway context.
The entrypoint reports ready and remains supervised instead of exiting after
startup requests. No plugin JavaScript is loaded by the native host.

Use it as the minimal structure in the [author guide](../../wiki/docs/plugin-author-guide.md).
Build/test with `pytest` and `python tools/build_packages.py`; inspect the isolated
`.validation/` distribution. New packages include this README, an icon, tags and
release-specific update metadata. Release signing requires a registered publisher.

plugins.readme:
# Plugin UI Playground

This demo uses a real Vue 3 frontend supplied by the plugin package.

It provides four pages, a private Discord webhook setting, and an **Announce this page to Discord** button on every page. The Vue app is loaded by the host in a sandboxed iframe and talks to the host through the plugin frontend bridge.

## Secret handling

The manifest requests `plugin.storage` and `notifications.send`.

The webhook is **not** stored in `ui.json` or ordinary plugin settings. The frontend sends it to the host's secret API, which stores it as `secrets/discord_webhook` in the plugin's private persistent data directory. The announce action never reads or echoes the webhook: it emits a Discord announcement request and the host runtime delivers it using the stored secret.

Plugin storage is private to the plugin runtime, quota-limited, path-confined, and written with owner-only file permissions. The frontend does not put the webhook in browser localStorage/sessionStorage.

Installation creates pending permission requests. The plugin remains disabled until the requested permissions are approved.

The frontend example uses a pinned Vue CDN script to keep this demo self-contained. A production plugin should normally ship a self-contained Vue/Vite build under `frontend/`.

## Where the pages appear

After installation and permission approval, open **Settings → Plugins → Plugin UI Playground** in Unnamed Tracking. The host embeds the plugin frontend in the plugin UI panel. The four plugin-owned pages are the tabs inside that embedded panel:

| Page | What to look for |
| --- | --- |
| **Overview** | The first/default tab; confirms the custom Vue frontend loaded. |
| **Library** | Plugin-rendered page showing its own page id; used to check tab switching. |
| **Details** | Plugin-rendered page showing its own page id; used to check tab switching. |
| **Diagnostics** | Plugin-rendered page showing its own page id; used to check tab switching. |

The **Discord announcement** controls appear below the current page. Enter a webhook, choose **Save webhook securely**, then use **Announce this page**. The action receives the current page context, so changing tabs and announcing should produce a different page name.

These are plugin-owned pages, not new top-level Unnamed Tracking routes. They should therefore remain inside the **Plugin UI Playground** panel under **Settings → Plugins**.

plugins.readme:
# User Invite Routing Demo

**Demo only.** This executes a synthetic issue → notification → confirmation flow through the public Plugin API 1.1.2. It never changes passwords, creates accounts, grants membership or returns destination addresses/credentials. SMTP belongs to the host. There is no anonymous recovery endpoint or production reset/invite implementation.

The `issue` action registers `example.user-invite-notification-demo.requested`, stores an expiring token digest under the authenticated user's storage key and emits typed facts. Its result contains acceptance/notification identity and expiry, never the token. The core handles preferences, destination selection, trust, urgency, retries and SMTP rendering. Required trust is **PRIVATE**, purpose **standard**. An enrolled PRIVATE email or authenticated inbox can receive this ordinary invitation demo; PUBLIC webhooks cannot.

With the plugin enabled and its declared permissions approved, call the authenticated host action API:

```http
POST /api/plugins/example.user-invite-notification-demo/actions/issue
Content-Type: application/json

{"values": {}}
```

Read the token from the eligible notification, then explicitly submit it:

```http
POST /api/plugins/example.user-invite-notification-demo/actions/confirm
Content-Type: application/json

{"values": {"token": "TOKEN_FROM_NOTIFICATION"}}
```

Both calls require the existing authenticated host session/API authorization. The sender cannot select another user/address. A new issue replaces the previous challenge; it expires after ten minutes. Confirmation consumes it sequentially and rejects another owner, replacement, expiry, alteration and sequential replay. Storage get/put is not a compare-and-swap transaction; concurrent confirmation is intentionally not a production authentication guarantee. No real authority is attached to the demo token.

Permissions are exactly source registration, notification emission and plugin storage. No full API, user enumeration, network access, host source imports or database access is requested. This is a protocol/action demonstration with no new frontend page; no screenshots apply.

From the companion repository root:

```sh
python -m pytest tests/test_notification_demos.py
python tools/check_source_layout.py
python tools/build_packages.py
```

Builds use the existing SDK/package format. Branch previews are unsigned and require explicit untrusted-package consent in the host. Signed main publication uses the existing demo signer; do not claim the source preview is a maintained official production auth plugin. Disable/uninstall retires source routing and queued work while the host retains notification history/preferences. Actual package/host acceptance is documented in the PR.

plugins.readme:
# Discord Bot Notifications

PRIVATE direct messages, optional host-verified SECURE recovery, and PUBLIC channel notifications using a dedicated Discord bot.

**Host requirement:** use a host with Plugin API 1.1.14 (rich embeds, edits and follow-ups; 1.1.11 is enough for the generic provider and native configuration UI only). Older hosts may reject registration or lack the required settings integrations. The updated source requires the independent destination-status read permission; transport and secrets remain plugin-owned.

## Per-account destinations

Use **Settings → Administration → Notifications** to configure **Discord account DM** with a dedicated bot token and server ID. These credentials belong to the plugin and are revision-bound separately from legacy native configuration. The token is write-only. This uses the provider's declared server fields, with no Discord-specific host settings.

In **Settings → Account → Notifications**, add one **Discord account DM** destination per exact Discord username in that server. Enrollment resolves a single Discord ID and remains PRIVATE; ordinary notifications work immediately, without a code. Changing the username or server configuration invalidates host proof and queued work. Merely renaming the Discord account does not change its saved target.

For SECURE delivery, separately approve the critical `notification_providers.sensitive` permission, then request and enter the host-generated code from that account's DM. Only the host confirms proof for that exact destination revision. Codes expire after ten minutes. Recovery delivery additionally requires the destination's explicit **Allow recovery messages** choice. This grant exposes verification codes and approved security/recovery content to this plugin; review it accordingly. Without the grant normal PRIVATE delivery still works.

Each attempt sends to exactly one account; missing, retired, changed or differently owned mappings fail instead of broadcasting. Temporary Discord/gateway failures are reported to the host retry queue. Oversized messages fail rather than truncating recovery secrets. The core owns all delivery state.

### Existing bot migration

The first maintained release is prepared for the existing signed catalogue publication workflow under **Unnamed Tracking Official**, with automatic updates disabled. Until publication succeeds and the bot appears in the catalogue, source/unsigned previews are not a published release.

If you installed an independently signed preview, uninstall it and freshly install the official package. Reconfigure credentials, activate destinations and repeat host verification and recovery consent. Do not use replacement installation to retain proof across signing identities. Existing preview credentials or verification must not be silently transferred to the official publisher.

The existing grouped **Discord Bot DM** provider and its native dashboard/account linking remain working as PRIVATE compatibility routes. Plugin link verification is not host SECURE proof. Existing links and tokens are retained and never automatically promoted or copied to the new provider. Configure the new per-account provider, explicitly activate and verify each desired account, then disable the old grouped provider to avoid receiving duplicate ordinary notices. Removing one new destination erases its plugin target into an opaque revision tombstone and leaves other accounts and legacy links intact. Reinstall requires fresh activation/configuration; old credentials cannot be reclaimed.

## Legacy setup

1. Create a dedicated bot application in the Discord Developer Portal. Keep its bot token private; never paste it into a chat or commit it to a repository.
2. Invite the bot to the Discord server that contains the users who want to link their accounts. Enable the **Server Members Intent** if Discord requires it for member search.
3. In **Settings → Administration → Discord Bot Notifications**, enter the bot token and that server's numeric ID. The plugin validates the credentials against Discord before saving. The token is write-only and is never returned by the status action.
4. Users can **Link for PRIVATE notifications** by username without a verification code. Optional legacy profile verification does not promote notification trust. The legacy grouped route remains PRIVATE.
5. For individual routes, configure **Discord account DM** under **Settings → Administration → Notifications**, then add one destination per username under **Settings → Account → Notifications**. Normal PRIVATE notifications work immediately. For SECURE/recovery delivery, complete the host-issued destination challenge, opt into recovery and grant the provider its separate high-risk permission.
6. Choose each destination under **Notification types**. The host applies trust, preferences, administrative policy and disclosure before handing approved content to the plugin.

Username enrollment resolves one exact member of the configured Discord server and stores its stable Discord ID. Zero or ambiguous matches are refused. Users may need to permit server-member DMs. Discord profile/account verification is not required for ordinary PRIVATE notifications.

## PUBLIC server channels

Administrators load the **Allowed notification channels and server users** directory in Discord bot administration. Text and announcement channels can be allowed individually. The member picker searches the loaded page; **Load more server users** retrieves the next page of up to 1,000 members. Administrators can link a selected Discord member to their own signed-in app account as PRIVATE; this does not change another app user's identity or prove access.

Configure the separate **Discord server channel** provider in **Administration → Notifications** using its bot token and server ID. Users then choose an allowed default channel in their Discord account settings and add a **Discord server channel** destination in **Account → Notifications**. Leave the destination's channel-ID field blank to use that selected default, or enter an allowed channel ID explicitly. Each destination retains its own channel: changing the default cannot reroute existing work. Per-type notification settings select which messages go to it.

Channels are always **PUBLIC**, including private Discord channels. Core PUBLIC release projections and generic tests may be delivered; private/security/recovery content cannot. Explicit richer media consent retains the host's field allowlist and never promotes trust. The plugin checks the administrator allowlist, server membership and text/announcement type at enrollment and each send. Removing a channel from the allowlist stops future deliveries immediately. The bot requires **View Channel** and **Send Messages**, including category/channel overrides. **Embed Links** enables rich notification cards. When Discord rejects a card with HTTP 403, the plugin tries the same approved content once as text in the same channel/DM, with automatic URL embeds and mentions disabled. Broader access failures still fail; rate limits, network errors and ambiguous server failures use the core retry policy without a second immediate send. Directory listing does not prove it can post.

Tokens remain write-only plugin storage; generic server configurations are separately revision-bound. Administrative channel/member discovery is not exposed to ordinary users; users see only allowed channels. Installations, user ownership, destination revisions and server revisions must match for every delivery. Deleted destinations retain target-free tombstones.

## Bot dashboard

The administrator page deliberately exposes as much non-secret Discord information as the bot can safely discover. It can show:

- bot username, global display name, Discord ID, avatar and verification state;
- a generated OAuth2 bot invite URL and the intents the plugin expects (`GUILDS` and `GUILD_MEMBERS`);
- Discord API health and measured plugin-side request time;
- server name, ID, icon, description, owner ID and vanity code;
- approximate total and online member counts;
- server verification level, boost tier/count, preferred locale and NSFW level;
- enabled Discord server features;
- AFK, system, rules and public-update channel IDs and related server settings when Discord exposes them;
- explicit-content filtering, default notification behavior, MFA level and widget state;
- the bot's server nickname, join time, pending state and assigned roles;
- the permissions calculated from the bot's effective server roles;
- the last successful user test DM and last successful notification delivery time for each linked account.

The dashboard never displays the bot token. Refreshing the dashboard re-queries Discord rather than relying on stale cached identity data.

## Security and behavior

- The bot token is stored in this plugin's private storage namespace, never returned to the frontend after saving, and can be cleared by an administrator. Treat the plugin's data volume as sensitive and back it up accordingly.
- Link codes expire after ten minutes and failed verification attempts are capped. The verification code is stored only as a hash.
- The legacy grouped provider remains PRIVATE and cannot receive verification/security/recovery content. The per-account provider becomes SECURE only after independent host proof and requires a separate high-risk handoff grant.
- The plugin sends DMs only to accounts linked by the same host account; PRIVATE enrollment does not require verification. Each per-account destination delivers only to its configured account. The legacy grouped provider broadcasts only to its remaining compatibility profile links. It disables Discord mention parsing in sent messages.
- The bot needs only the server access required by this integration. Member discovery uses the Discord member list and therefore may require the Server Members Intent. Keep the token dedicated to this integration and rotate it if exposed.
- Discord API calls use the plugin's declared `network.outbound` capability through the bounded host gateway. The plugin owns the external Discord network calls and credentials.
- Notification bodies are bounded before sending and the bot does not interpret notification text as mentions.
- User links are scoped by the authenticated host user ID inside plugin storage; the host does not receive the Discord credential or own the Discord account mapping.

The plugin declares its PRIVATE account and PUBLIC channel providers, fields, features, privacy and configuration/delivery actions through the existing generic provider API. The host does not need Discord-specific credential handling or delivery code.

The native link page now supports **Link for PRIVATE notifications** without receiving a code. Optional legacy profile proof does not upgrade destination trust. For recovery use the separate **Discord account DM** destination in Account → Notifications, host verification, recovery opt-in and the high-risk delivery grant. The administrator must configure its revision-bound server fields in Admin → Notifications. DMs use native rich cards; Discord does not render email HTML. The maintained release uses the registered **Unnamed Tracking Official** publisher and keeps **manual updates**.

All DMs use native rich cards with spaced paragraphs, an emphasized verification code and a short **here** action link. HTTP delivery does not show the bot as online: persistent Discord Gateway presence is deferred until the host exposes an approved WebSocket transport with connection/heartbeat/reconnect lifecycle. Direct sockets are unavailable in the isolated plugin runtime.


Text fallback uses spaced paragraphs and named links (View notification, Reset
your password, Accept invitation or Verify destination). It reserves room for a
complete action rather than truncating its URL. Local previews keep their local
URL; deployed notifications use the host-resolved notification URL. An action too
long to fit is omitted whole with a prompt to open the app.

## Trust, recovery and searchable selection

The account page reads actual destination trust from the host through the separate
`notification_destinations.read` permission (API 1.1.11). It shows PRIVATE and SECURE
destinations separately, with current password-reset routing readiness. Existing profile
links are collapsed as **Compatibility profile links**; their optional profile verification
does not make a notification destination SECURE. No destination addresses, host secrets,
challenge codes, notification content or other providers' destinations are returned by
this read API. Local Discord labels are added only from this plugin's matching actor and
destination revision. Failed refresh clears old trust badges.

Use **Verify DM and configure recovery** for the exact host destination. Complete its
host challenge, then enable **Allow recovery messages**. The separate sensitive-content
permission must be granted, and the administrator must enable the password-reset plugin.
The card explains missing proof, opt-in, permission, availability or routing. A verified
destination can still have recovery disabled. PUBLIC channels never receive reset secrets.
Host verification and recovery controls retain authority; this plugin cannot promote trust.

Administrators can use **Find bot servers**, search by name or ID, select the bot's server
or enter an ID manually. Discovery uses the entered write-only token or the stored native
compatibility token, and returns at most 100 servers per request, with explicit pagination.
It uses Discord's [Get Current User Guilds](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/user#get-current-user-guilds)
endpoint; large bot sharding is outside this single-server integration. Selecting a server
does not save until **Validate and save**. This section configures the directory and legacy
grouped provider; links open the separately revision-bound DM/channel provider settings in
Administration → Notifications. Changing those server settings retires previous destinations
and requires explicit reconfiguration and new host proof.

Channel allowlists, allowed user channels, members and destination/account cards support
name/ID search. Member search covers loaded pages; **Load more server users** expands the
directory. Bulk matching channel selection preserves hidden choices until an explicit save.
User channels remain administrator-allowed PUBLIC targets. Each existing destination keeps
its own target; selecting a default channel only affects future enrollment.

Version 0.1.1 is a manual update requiring API 1.1.11 and permission review. Earlier packages
and signing history remain immutable. Install/update the host before updating the bot.

## Activity identity adapter (0.1.2 preview)

The separate Game Night Activity requires the API 1.1.12 host and this updated
adapter. Existing notification links and destinations keep their behavior. The
Activity does not inherit their notification or recovery authority.

Grant `integrations.identity_provider` explicitly and configure **Discord Activity
sign-in** on the administrator page with the bot's application ID and OAuth2
client secret. The bot token and OAuth client secret are different credentials;
both remain in write-only private plugin storage. The configured bot must belong
to that application. A saved client secret is never returned to the UI.

The adapter exchanges the SDK authorization code, reads the OAuth user's verified
identity, and checks their membership in the same Discord Activity instance and
configured guild. Revalidation repeats the membership check. A claimed user or
room supplied by the browser cannot replace this proof. Verified avatar URLs
include Discord's default-avatar fallback; the host retrieves raster images
through its bounded image transport.

Configure root and `/api` Activity URL mappings as described in the
[Game Night README](../discord-social-activity/README.md). Each operator currently
uses their own application. This preview does not create a persistent Gateway
connection or change the existing bot notification delivery implementation.

Operators can explicitly allow **Activities in DMs and group DMs** in Activity
sign-in settings (default off). The verified Activity location must be Discord's
private-channel kind, with a valid channel and exact connected member. Guild
rooms remain restricted to the configured server. Saving this policy can retain
the existing secret by leaving its field blank for the same application ID.
Private Activity participation is separate from notification DM enrollment.

## Rich batches and editable story messages (host Plugin API 1.1.14)

The per-account DM and server-channel providers declare presentation capabilities and an edit
action (`edit-account`, `edit-channel`). `sdk/discord_embeds.py` renders host-approved facts,
images, links and action links as embeds with link buttons (the live story page first, at most 5),
a digest of up to 8 items as one message (one embed per item, "And N more" plus the story link
beyond that) and keeps every message inside Discord's limits (10 embeds, 6,000 characters in
total, 256/4,096/1,024 for title/description/field value, 25 fields). Truncation is
deterministic; mentions never notify; only http(s) links survive.

* **Message references.** A created message is returned to the host as an opaque
  `channel_id:message_id` reference. For an edit the provider re-checks the destination
  revision, owner, server revision and (for channels) the administrator allowlist exactly as
  for a send, then requires the reference's channel to be this destination's channel (for a DM,
  the channel opened for the currently linked account) before `PATCH`ing it. A foreign
  reference, another bot's message (HTTP 403) or a deleted one (404) is reported as `gone`; the
  host then sends a follow-up, threaded with `message_reference` when the original still exists.
* **Isolation and revocation.** Each destination uses the bot token of its own installation
  server record; a retired, re-routed, re-linked or stale-revision destination makes no Discord
  call at all, so revoked or unlinked destinations receive no later updates.
* **Retries.** The host's idempotency key becomes the Discord `nonce` (with `enforce_nonce`), so a
  crash after Discord accepted a message cannot post it twice. 429 and 5xx/network failures are
  retryable and create nothing; a 403 on create falls back once to plain text with previews
  suppressed (missing Embed Links), as before. Other failures are permanent and per delivery.
* **Privacy.** Channels stay PUBLIC and DMs PRIVATE. The provider renders only the fields the
  host supplied for the destination's projection; facts, HTML and identifiers the host did not
  send for a PUBLIC projection cannot appear. Tests/verification/recovery keep the previous
  minimal path. The legacy grouped `.dm` provider is unchanged.

Release order: host (Plugin API 1.1.14) first, then this package.

# Discord Bot Notifications

PRIVATE direct messages, optional host-verified SECURE recovery, and PUBLIC channel notifications using a dedicated Discord bot.

**Host requirement:** use a host with Plugin API 1.1.11 for the current generic provider and native configuration UI. Older hosts may reject registration or lack the required settings integrations. The updated source requires the independent destination-status read permission; transport and secrets remain plugin-owned.

## Per-account destinations

Use **Settings → Administration → Notifications** to configure **Discord account DM** with a dedicated bot token and server ID. These credentials belong to the plugin and are revision-bound separately from legacy native configuration. The token is write-only. This uses the provider's declared server fields, with no Discord-specific host settings.

In **Settings → Account → Notifications**, add one **Discord account DM** destination per exact Discord username in that server. Enrollment resolves a single Discord ID and remains PRIVATE; ordinary notifications work immediately, without a code. Changing the username or server configuration invalidates host proof and queued work. Merely renaming the Discord account does not change its saved target.

For SECURE delivery, separately approve the critical `notification_providers.sensitive` permission, then request and enter the host-generated code from that account's DM. Only the host confirms proof for that exact destination revision. Codes expire after ten minutes. Recovery delivery additionally requires the destination's explicit **Allow recovery messages** choice. This grant exposes verification codes and approved security/recovery content to this plugin; review it accordingly. Without the grant normal PRIVATE delivery still works.

Each attempt sends to exactly one account; missing, retired, changed or differently owned mappings fail instead of broadcasting. Temporary Discord/gateway failures are reported to the host retry queue. Oversized messages fail rather than truncating recovery secrets. The core owns all delivery state.

### Existing bot migration

The first maintained release is prepared for the existing signed catalogue publication workflow under **Unnamed Tracking Official**, with automatic updates disabled. Until publication succeeds and the bot appears in the catalogue, source/unsigned previews are not a published release.

If you installed an independently signed preview, uninstall it and freshly install the official package. Reconfigure credentials, activate destinations and repeat host verification and recovery consent. Do not use replacement installation to retain proof across signing identities. Existing preview credentials or verification must not be silently transferred to the official publisher.

The existing grouped **Discord Bot DM** provider and its native dashboard/account linking remain working as PRIVATE compatibility routes. Plugin link verification is not host SECURE proof. Existing links and tokens are retained and never automatically promoted or copied to the new provider. Configure the new per-account provider, explicitly activate and verify each desired account, then disable the old grouped provider to avoid receiving duplicate ordinary notices. Removing one new destination erases its plugin target into an opaque revision tombstone and leaves other accounts and legacy links intact. Reinstall requires fresh activation/configuration; old credentials cannot be reclaimed.

## Legacy setup

1. Create a dedicated bot application in the Discord Developer Portal. Keep its bot token private; never paste it into a chat or commit it to a repository.
2. Invite the bot to the Discord server that contains the users who want to link their accounts. Enable the **Server Members Intent** if Discord requires it for member search.
3. In **Settings → Administration → Discord Bot Notifications**, enter the bot token and that server's numeric ID. The plugin validates the credentials against Discord before saving. The token is write-only and is never returned by the status action.
4. Users can **Link for PRIVATE notifications** by username without a verification code. Optional legacy profile verification does not promote notification trust. The legacy grouped route remains PRIVATE.
5. For individual routes, configure **Discord account DM** under **Settings → Administration → Notifications**, then add one destination per username under **Settings → Account → Notifications**. Normal PRIVATE notifications work immediately. For SECURE/recovery delivery, complete the host-issued destination challenge, opt into recovery and grant the provider its separate high-risk permission.
6. Choose each destination under **Notification types**. The host applies trust, preferences, administrative policy and disclosure before handing approved content to the plugin.

Username enrollment resolves one exact member of the configured Discord server and stores its stable Discord ID. Zero or ambiguous matches are refused. Users may need to permit server-member DMs. Discord profile/account verification is not required for ordinary PRIVATE notifications.

## PUBLIC server channels

Administrators load the **Allowed notification channels and server users** directory in Discord bot administration. Text and announcement channels can be allowed individually. The member picker searches the loaded page; **Load more server users** retrieves the next page of up to 1,000 members. Administrators can link a selected Discord member to their own signed-in app account as PRIVATE; this does not change another app user's identity or prove access.

Configure the separate **Discord server channel** provider in **Administration → Notifications** using its bot token and server ID. Users then choose an allowed default channel in their Discord account settings and add a **Discord server channel** destination in **Account → Notifications**. Leave the destination's channel-ID field blank to use that selected default, or enter an allowed channel ID explicitly. Each destination retains its own channel: changing the default cannot reroute existing work. Per-type notification settings select which messages go to it.

Channels are always **PUBLIC**, including private Discord channels. Core PUBLIC release projections and generic tests may be delivered; private/security/recovery content cannot. Explicit richer media consent retains the host's field allowlist and never promotes trust. The plugin checks the administrator allowlist, server membership and text/announcement type at enrollment and each send. Removing a channel from the allowlist stops future deliveries immediately. The bot requires **View Channel** and **Send Messages**, including category/channel overrides. **Embed Links** enables rich notification cards. When Discord rejects a card with HTTP 403, the plugin tries the same approved content once as text in the same channel/DM, with automatic URL embeds and mentions disabled. Broader access failures still fail; rate limits, network errors and ambiguous server failures use the core retry policy without a second immediate send. Directory listing does not prove it can post.

Tokens remain write-only plugin storage; generic server configurations are separately revision-bound. Administrative channel/member discovery is not exposed to ordinary users; users see only allowed channels. Installations, user ownership, destination revisions and server revisions must match for every delivery. Deleted destinations retain target-free tombstones.

## Bot dashboard

The administrator page deliberately exposes as much non-secret Discord information as the bot can safely discover. It can show:

- bot username, global display name, Discord ID, avatar and verification state;
- a generated OAuth2 bot invite URL and the intents the plugin expects (`GUILDS` and `GUILD_MEMBERS`);
- Discord API health and measured plugin-side request time;
- server name, ID, icon, description, owner ID and vanity code;
- approximate total and online member counts;
- server verification level, boost tier/count, preferred locale and NSFW level;
- enabled Discord server features;
- AFK, system, rules and public-update channel IDs and related server settings when Discord exposes them;
- explicit-content filtering, default notification behavior, MFA level and widget state;
- the bot's server nickname, join time, pending state and assigned roles;
- the permissions calculated from the bot's effective server roles;
- the last successful user test DM and last successful notification delivery time for each linked account.

The dashboard never displays the bot token. Refreshing the dashboard re-queries Discord rather than relying on stale cached identity data.

## Security and behavior

- The bot token is stored in this plugin's private storage namespace, never returned to the frontend after saving, and can be cleared by an administrator. Treat the plugin's data volume as sensitive and back it up accordingly.
- Link codes expire after ten minutes and failed verification attempts are capped. The verification code is stored only as a hash.
- The legacy grouped provider remains PRIVATE and cannot receive verification/security/recovery content. The per-account provider becomes SECURE only after independent host proof and requires a separate high-risk handoff grant.
- The plugin sends DMs only to accounts linked by the same host account; PRIVATE enrollment does not require verification. Each per-account destination delivers only to its configured account. The legacy grouped provider broadcasts only to its remaining compatibility profile links. It disables Discord mention parsing in sent messages.
- The bot needs only the server access required by this integration. Member discovery uses the Discord member list and therefore may require the Server Members Intent. Keep the token dedicated to this integration and rotate it if exposed.
- Discord API calls use the plugin's declared `network.outbound` capability through the bounded host gateway. The plugin owns the external Discord network calls and credentials.
- Notification bodies are bounded before sending and the bot does not interpret notification text as mentions.
- User links are scoped by the authenticated host user ID inside plugin storage; the host does not receive the Discord credential or own the Discord account mapping.

The plugin declares its PRIVATE account and PUBLIC channel providers, fields, features, privacy and configuration/delivery actions through the existing generic provider API. The host does not need Discord-specific credential handling or delivery code.

The native link page now supports **Link for PRIVATE notifications** without receiving a code. Optional legacy profile proof does not upgrade destination trust. For recovery use the separate **Discord account DM** destination in Account → Notifications, host verification, recovery opt-in and the high-risk delivery grant. The administrator must configure its revision-bound server fields in Admin → Notifications. DMs use native rich cards; Discord does not render email HTML. The maintained release uses the registered **Unnamed Tracking Official** publisher and keeps **manual updates**.

All DMs use native rich cards with spaced paragraphs, an emphasized verification code and a short **here** action link. HTTP delivery does not show the bot as online: persistent Discord Gateway presence is deferred until the host exposes an approved WebSocket transport with connection/heartbeat/reconnect lifecycle. Direct sockets are unavailable in the isolated plugin runtime.


Text fallback uses spaced paragraphs and named links (View notification, Reset
your password, Accept invitation or Verify destination). It reserves room for a
complete action rather than truncating its URL. Local previews keep their local
URL; deployed notifications use the host-resolved notification URL. An action too
long to fit is omitted whole with a prompt to open the app.

## Trust, recovery and searchable selection

The account page reads actual destination trust from the host through the separate
`notification_destinations.read` permission (API 1.1.11). It shows PRIVATE and SECURE
destinations separately, with current password-reset routing readiness. Existing profile
links are collapsed as **Compatibility profile links**; their optional profile verification
does not make a notification destination SECURE. No destination addresses, host secrets,
challenge codes, notification content or other providers' destinations are returned by
this read API. Local Discord labels are added only from this plugin's matching actor and
destination revision. Failed refresh clears old trust badges.

Use **Verify DM and configure recovery** for the exact host destination. Complete its
host challenge, then enable **Allow recovery messages**. The separate sensitive-content
permission must be granted, and the administrator must enable the password-reset plugin.
The card explains missing proof, opt-in, permission, availability or routing. A verified
destination can still have recovery disabled. PUBLIC channels never receive reset secrets.
Host verification and recovery controls retain authority; this plugin cannot promote trust.

Administrators can use **Find bot servers**, search by name or ID, select the bot's server
or enter an ID manually. Discovery uses the entered write-only token or the stored native
compatibility token, and returns at most 100 servers per request, with explicit pagination.
It uses Discord's [Get Current User Guilds](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/user#get-current-user-guilds)
endpoint; large bot sharding is outside this single-server integration. Selecting a server
does not save until **Validate and save**. This section configures the directory and legacy
grouped provider; links open the separately revision-bound DM/channel provider settings in
Administration → Notifications. Changing those server settings retires previous destinations
and requires explicit reconfiguration and new host proof.

Channel allowlists, allowed user channels, members and destination/account cards support
name/ID search. Member search covers loaded pages; **Load more server users** expands the
directory. Bulk matching channel selection preserves hidden choices until an explicit save.
User channels remain administrator-allowed PUBLIC targets. Each existing destination keeps
its own target; selecting a default channel only affects future enrollment.

Version 0.1.1 is a manual update requiring API 1.1.11 and permission review. Earlier packages
and signing history remain immutable. Install/update the host before updating the bot.

## Activity identity adapter (0.1.2 preview)

The separate Game Night Activity requires the API 1.1.12 host and this updated
adapter. Existing notification links and destinations keep their behavior. The
Activity does not inherit their notification or recovery authority.

Grant `integrations.identity_provider` explicitly and configure **Discord Activity
sign-in** on the administrator page with the bot's application ID and OAuth2
client secret. The bot token and OAuth client secret are different credentials;
both remain in write-only private plugin storage. The configured bot must belong
to that application. A saved client secret is never returned to the UI.

The adapter exchanges the SDK authorization code, reads the OAuth user's verified
identity, and checks their membership in the same Discord Activity instance and
configured guild. Revalidation repeats the membership check. A claimed user or
room supplied by the browser cannot replace this proof. Verified avatar URLs
include Discord's default-avatar fallback; the host retrieves raster images
through its bounded image transport.

Configure root and `/api` Activity URL mappings as described in the
[Game Night README](../discord-social-activity/README.md). Each operator currently
uses their own application. This preview does not create a persistent Gateway
connection or change the existing bot notification delivery implementation.

Operators can explicitly allow **Activities in DMs and group DMs** in Activity
sign-in settings (default off). The verified Activity location must be Discord's
private-channel kind, with a valid channel and exact connected member. Guild
rooms remain restricted to the configured server. Saving this policy can retain
the existing secret by leaving its field blank for the same application ID.
Private Activity participation is separate from notification DM enrollment.
