# Discord Bot Notifications

PRIVATE direct messages, optional host-verified SECURE recovery, and PUBLIC channel notifications using a dedicated Discord bot.

**Host requirement:** use a host with Plugin API 1.1.14 (rich embeds, edits and follow-ups; 1.1.11 is enough for the generic provider and native configuration UI only). Older hosts may reject registration or lack the required settings integrations. The updated source requires the independent destination-status read permission; transport and secrets remain plugin-owned.

## Per-account destinations

Use **Settings → Administration → Notifications** to configure **Discord account DM** with a dedicated bot token and server ID. These credentials belong to the plugin and are revision-bound separately from legacy native configuration. The token is write-only. This uses the provider's declared server fields, with no Discord-specific host settings.

In **Settings → Account → Notifications**, add one **Discord account DM** destination per exact Discord username in that server. Enrollment resolves a single Discord ID and remains PRIVATE; ordinary notifications work immediately, without a code. Changing the username or server configuration invalidates host proof and queued work. Merely renaming the Discord account does not change its saved target.

For SECURE delivery, separately approve the critical `notification_providers.sensitive` permission, then request and enter the host-generated code from that account's DM. Only the host confirms proof for that exact destination revision. Codes expire after ten minutes. Recovery delivery additionally requires the destination's explicit **Allow recovery messages** choice. This grant exposes verification codes and approved security/recovery content to this plugin; review it accordingly. Without the grant normal PRIVATE delivery still works.

Each attempt sends to exactly one account; missing, retired, changed or differently owned mappings fail instead of broadcasting. Temporary Discord/gateway failures are reported to the host retry queue. Oversized messages fail rather than truncating recovery secrets. The core owns all delivery state.

### Existing bot migration

The first maintained release is prepared for the existing signed catalogue publication workflow under **Unnamed Tracking Official**, with automatic updates disabled. Until publication succeeds and the bot appears in the catalogue, source/unsigned previews are not a published release.

If you installed an independently signed preview, uninstall it and freshly install the official package. Reconfigure credentials, activate destinations and repeat host verification and recovery consent. Do not use replacement installation to retain proof across signing identities. Existing preview credentials or verification must not be silently transferred to the official publisher.

The existing grouped **Discord Bot DM** provider and its native dashboard/account linking remain working as PRIVATE compatibility routes. Plugin link verification is not host SECURE proof. Existing links and tokens are retained and never automatically promoted or copied to the new provider. Configure the new per-account provider, explicitly activate and verify each desired account, then disable the old grouped provider to avoid receiving duplicate ordinary notices. Removing one new destination erases its plugin target into an opaque revision tombstone and leaves other accounts and legacy links intact. Reinstall requires fresh activation/configuration; old credentials cannot be reclaimed.

## Legacy setup

1. Create a dedicated bot application in the Discord Developer Portal. Keep its bot token private; never paste it into a chat or commit it to a repository.
2. Invite the bot to the Discord server that contains the users who want to link their accounts. Enable the **Server Members Intent** if Discord requires it for member search.
3. In **Settings → Administration → Discord Bot Notifications**, enter the bot token and that server's numeric ID. The plugin validates the credentials against Discord before saving. The token is write-only and is never returned by the status action.
4. Users can **Link for PRIVATE notifications** by username without a verification code. Optional legacy profile verification does not promote notification trust. The legacy grouped route remains PRIVATE.
5. For individual routes, configure **Discord account DM** under **Settings → Administration → Notifications**, then add one destination per username under **Settings → Account → Notifications**. Normal PRIVATE notifications work immediately. For SECURE/recovery delivery, complete the host-issued destination challenge, opt into recovery and grant the provider its separate high-risk permission.
6. Choose each destination under **Notification types**. The host applies trust, preferences, administrative policy and disclosure before handing approved content to the plugin.

Username enrollment resolves one exact member of the configured Discord server and stores its stable Discord ID. Zero or ambiguous matches are refused. Users may need to permit server-member DMs. Discord profile/account verification is not required for ordinary PRIVATE notifications.

## PUBLIC server channels

Administrators load the **Allowed notification channels and server users** directory in Discord bot administration. Text and announcement channels can be allowed individually. The member picker searches the loaded page; **Load more server users** retrieves the next page of up to 1,000 members. Administrators can link a selected Discord member to their own signed-in app account as PRIVATE; this does not change another app user's identity or prove access.

Configure the separate **Discord server channel** provider in **Administration → Notifications** using its bot token and server ID. Users then choose an allowed default channel in their Discord account settings and add a **Discord server channel** destination in **Account → Notifications**. Leave the destination's channel-ID field blank to use that selected default, or enter an allowed channel ID explicitly. Each destination retains its own channel: changing the default cannot reroute existing work. Per-type notification settings select which messages go to it.

Channels are always **PUBLIC**, including private Discord channels. Core PUBLIC release projections and generic tests may be delivered; private/security/recovery content cannot. Explicit richer media consent retains the host's field allowlist and never promotes trust. The plugin checks the administrator allowlist, server membership and text/announcement type at enrollment and each send. Removing a channel from the allowlist stops future deliveries immediately. The bot requires **View Channel** and **Send Messages**, including category/channel overrides. **Embed Links** enables rich notification cards. When Discord rejects a card with HTTP 403, the plugin tries the same approved content once as text in the same channel/DM, with automatic URL embeds and mentions disabled. Broader access failures still fail; rate limits, network errors and ambiguous server failures use the core retry policy without a second immediate send. Directory listing does not prove it can post.

Tokens remain write-only plugin storage; generic server configurations are separately revision-bound. Administrative channel/member discovery is not exposed to ordinary users; users see only allowed channels. Installations, user ownership, destination revisions and server revisions must match for every delivery. Deleted destinations retain target-free tombstones.

## Bot dashboard

The administrator page deliberately exposes as much non-secret Discord information as the bot can safely discover. It can show:

- bot username, global display name, Discord ID, avatar and verification state;
- a generated OAuth2 bot invite URL and the intents the plugin expects (`GUILDS` and `GUILD_MEMBERS`);
- Discord API health and measured plugin-side request time;
- server name, ID, icon, description, owner ID and vanity code;
- approximate total and online member counts;
- server verification level, boost tier/count, preferred locale and NSFW level;
- enabled Discord server features;
- AFK, system, rules and public-update channel IDs and related server settings when Discord exposes them;
- explicit-content filtering, default notification behavior, MFA level and widget state;
- the bot's server nickname, join time, pending state and assigned roles;
- the permissions calculated from the bot's effective server roles;
- the last successful user test DM and last successful notification delivery time for each linked account.

The dashboard never displays the bot token. Refreshing the dashboard re-queries Discord rather than relying on stale cached identity data.

## Security and behavior

- The bot token is stored in this plugin's private storage namespace, never returned to the frontend after saving, and can be cleared by an administrator. Treat the plugin's data volume as sensitive and back it up accordingly.
- Link codes expire after ten minutes and failed verification attempts are capped. The verification code is stored only as a hash.
- The legacy grouped provider remains PRIVATE and cannot receive verification/security/recovery content. The per-account provider becomes SECURE only after independent host proof and requires a separate high-risk handoff grant.
- The plugin sends DMs only to accounts linked by the same host account; PRIVATE enrollment does not require verification. Each per-account destination delivers only to its configured account. The legacy grouped provider broadcasts only to its remaining compatibility profile links. It disables Discord mention parsing in sent messages.
- The bot needs only the server access required by this integration. Member discovery uses the Discord member list and therefore may require the Server Members Intent. Keep the token dedicated to this integration and rotate it if exposed.
- Discord API calls use the plugin's declared `network.outbound` capability through the bounded host gateway. The plugin owns the external Discord network calls and credentials.
- Notification bodies are bounded before sending and the bot does not interpret notification text as mentions.
- User links are scoped by the authenticated host user ID inside plugin storage; the host does not receive the Discord credential or own the Discord account mapping.

The plugin declares its PRIVATE account and PUBLIC channel providers, fields, features, privacy and configuration/delivery actions through the existing generic provider API. The host does not need Discord-specific credential handling or delivery code.

The native link page now supports **Link for PRIVATE notifications** without receiving a code. Optional legacy profile proof does not upgrade destination trust. For recovery use the separate **Discord account DM** destination in Account → Notifications, host verification, recovery opt-in and the high-risk delivery grant. The administrator must configure its revision-bound server fields in Admin → Notifications. DMs use native rich cards; Discord does not render email HTML. The maintained release uses the registered **Unnamed Tracking Official** publisher and keeps **manual updates**.

All DMs use native rich cards with spaced paragraphs, an emphasized verification code and a short **here** action link. HTTP delivery does not show the bot as online: persistent Discord Gateway presence is deferred until the host exposes an approved WebSocket transport with connection/heartbeat/reconnect lifecycle. Direct sockets are unavailable in the isolated plugin runtime.


Text fallback uses spaced paragraphs and named links (View notification, Reset
your password, Accept invitation or Verify destination). It reserves room for a
complete action rather than truncating its URL. Local previews keep their local
URL; deployed notifications use the host-resolved notification URL. An action too
long to fit is omitted whole with a prompt to open the app.

## Trust, recovery and searchable selection

The account page reads actual destination trust from the host through the separate
`notification_destinations.read` permission (API 1.1.11). It shows PRIVATE and SECURE
destinations separately, with current password-reset routing readiness. Existing profile
links are collapsed as **Compatibility profile links**; their optional profile verification
does not make a notification destination SECURE. No destination addresses, host secrets,
challenge codes, notification content or other providers' destinations are returned by
this read API. Local Discord labels are added only from this plugin's matching actor and
destination revision. Failed refresh clears old trust badges.

Use **Verify DM and configure recovery** for the exact host destination. Complete its
host challenge, then enable **Allow recovery messages**. The separate sensitive-content
permission must be granted, and the administrator must enable the password-reset plugin.
The card explains missing proof, opt-in, permission, availability or routing. A verified
destination can still have recovery disabled. PUBLIC channels never receive reset secrets.
Host verification and recovery controls retain authority; this plugin cannot promote trust.

Administrators can use **Find bot servers**, search by name or ID, select the bot's server
or enter an ID manually. Discovery uses the entered write-only token or the stored native
compatibility token, and returns at most 100 servers per request, with explicit pagination.
It uses Discord's [Get Current User Guilds](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/user#get-current-user-guilds)
endpoint; large bot sharding is outside this single-server integration. Selecting a server
does not save until **Validate and save**. This section configures the directory and legacy
grouped provider; links open the separately revision-bound DM/channel provider settings in
Administration → Notifications. Changing those server settings retires previous destinations
and requires explicit reconfiguration and new host proof.

Channel allowlists, allowed user channels, members and destination/account cards support
name/ID search. Member search covers loaded pages; **Load more server users** expands the
directory. Bulk matching channel selection preserves hidden choices until an explicit save.
User channels remain administrator-allowed PUBLIC targets. Each existing destination keeps
its own target; selecting a default channel only affects future enrollment.

Version 0.1.1 is a manual update requiring API 1.1.11 and permission review. Earlier packages
and signing history remain immutable. Install/update the host before updating the bot.

## Activity identity adapter (0.1.2 preview)

The separate Game Night Activity requires the API 1.1.12 host and this updated
adapter. Existing notification links and destinations keep their behavior. The
Activity does not inherit their notification or recovery authority.

Grant `integrations.identity_provider` explicitly and configure **Discord Activity
sign-in** on the administrator page with the bot's application ID and OAuth2
client secret. The bot token and OAuth client secret are different credentials;
both remain in write-only private plugin storage. The configured bot must belong
to that application. A saved client secret is never returned to the UI.

The adapter exchanges the SDK authorization code, reads the OAuth user's verified
identity, and checks their membership in the same Discord Activity instance and
configured guild. Revalidation repeats the membership check. A claimed user or
room supplied by the browser cannot replace this proof. Verified avatar URLs
include Discord's default-avatar fallback; the host retrieves raster images
through its bounded image transport.

Configure root and `/api` Activity URL mappings as described in the
[Game Night README](../discord-social-activity/README.md). Each operator currently
uses their own application. This preview does not create a persistent Gateway
connection or change the existing bot notification delivery implementation.

Operators can explicitly allow **Activities in DMs and group DMs** in Activity
sign-in settings (default off). The verified Activity location must be Discord's
private-channel kind, with a valid channel and exact connected member. Guild
rooms remain restricted to the configured server. Saving this policy can retain
the existing secret by leaving its field blank for the same application ID.
Private Activity participation is separate from notification DM enrollment.

## Rich batches and editable story messages (host Plugin API 1.1.14)

The per-account DM and server-channel providers declare presentation capabilities and an edit
action (`edit-account`, `edit-channel`). `sdk/discord_embeds.py` renders host-approved facts,
images, links and action links as embeds with link buttons (the live story page first, at most 5),
a digest of up to 8 items as one message (one embed per item, "And N more" plus the story link
beyond that) and keeps every message inside Discord's limits (10 embeds, 6,000 characters in
total, 256/4,096/1,024 for title/description/field value, 25 fields). Truncation is
deterministic; mentions never notify; only http(s) links survive.

* **Message references.** A created message is returned to the host as an opaque
  `channel_id:message_id` reference. For an edit the provider re-checks the destination
  revision, owner, server revision and (for channels) the administrator allowlist exactly as
  for a send, then requires the reference's channel to be this destination's channel (for a DM,
  the channel opened for the currently linked account) before `PATCH`ing it. A foreign
  reference, another bot's message (HTTP 403) or a deleted one (404) is reported as `gone`; the
  host then sends a follow-up, threaded with `message_reference` when the original still exists.
* **Isolation and revocation.** Each destination uses the bot token of its own installation
  server record; a retired, re-routed, re-linked or stale-revision destination makes no Discord
  call at all, so revoked or unlinked destinations receive no later updates.
* **Retries.** The host's idempotency key becomes the Discord `nonce` (with `enforce_nonce`), so a
  crash after Discord accepted a message cannot post it twice. 429 and 5xx/network failures are
  retryable and create nothing; a 403 on create falls back once to plain text with previews
  suppressed (missing Embed Links), as before. Other failures are permanent and per delivery.
* **Privacy.** Channels stay PUBLIC and DMs PRIVATE. The provider renders only the fields the
  host supplied for the destination's projection; facts, HTML and identifiers the host did not
  send for a PUBLIC projection cannot appear. Tests/verification/recovery keep the previous
  minimal path. The legacy grouped `.dm` provider is unchanged.

Release order: host (Plugin API 1.1.14) first, then this package.

# Discord Webhook Notifications

Maintained Discord webhook delivery through the generic provider contract (rich delivery needs Plugin API 1.1.14).
Deploy the paired host provider/settings change before installing this release.

## Setup

1. Install the plugin and approve its provider, storage and outbound-network grants.
2. Open the host's notification settings and enable Discord Webhook for your account.
3. Add a destination using the generated configuration form. Enter a label and an
   ordinary Discord text-channel webhook URL. Multiple destinations are supported.
4. Choose notification types and use **Send test notification** to exercise the
   configured credentials through the core dispatcher.

Webhooks remain PUBLIC. Default media announcements contain public release facts.
Each destination revision can separately opt into the richer followed-media
projection; this does not permit account identifiers, watch history, ratings or
security content. Critical urgency is not supported by this provider.

## Configuration and delivery

The plugin declares its fields, destination kind and features; the host renders
them with shared controls. The plugin validates and stores its own webhook tokens
under opaque installation/destination IDs and revisions. Credentials are never
returned to forms, action results, lifecycle records or host notification rows.
Editing retains an omitted saved URL, invalidates pending work and clears previous
media consent. Removal deletes the URL and retains only a revision tombstone.

Only exact HTTPS discord.com/discordapp.com webhook paths are accepted, without
userinfo, alternate ports, query parameters or fragments. The plugin uses its own
bounded network grant and renders only core-approved content with mentions disabled.
Empty successful Discord responses are accepted; rate limits and server/network
failures are retryable, while invalid/revoked webhook responses fail permanently.
Core owns delivery state, leases, retries, preferences and routing checks.

## Rich batches and editable story messages (host Plugin API 1.1.14)

The webhook declares presentation capabilities (`rich_embeds`, edits, up to 8 digest items,
4 images, link actions) and an `edit` action. Canonical deliveries are laid out by
`sdk/discord_embeds.py` within Discord's hard limits: at most 10 embeds and 6,000 characters
per message, 256/4,096 characters for title/description and 25 fields of 256/1,024 characters.
Truncation is deterministic, a cut description always ends with the live story link, mentions
never notify (`allowed_mentions` parses nothing) and only http(s) links survive. Webhooks cannot
carry buttons, so actions are listed as links in the embed.

Messages are created with `?wait=true`; Discord's message id is returned to the host as the opaque
reference. A later story revision edits that message (`PATCH .../messages/{id}`) while the host
decides it is eligible; a deleted message (HTTP 404/403) is reported as `gone` and the host
sends a selective follow-up instead. Webhook messages cannot be replied to, so follow-ups are
standalone. A reference only works with the webhook that created it. The host-owned test message
keeps the minimal payload. Rate limits (429) and 5xx/network errors are retryable; other errors
fail without blocking other providers. Release order: host (Plugin API 1.1.14) first, then this
package.

## Migration and testing

This release requires explicit enrollment. Historical protected webhook secrets
are not transferred to plugin storage, and automatic update is disabled for this
transition. Old packages remain immutable and notification history is retained.

Standalone source and generated-package tests cover field validation, installation
separation, revision races, secret removal, malformed URLs, approved content and
HTTP failure handling. No production Discord credential is required by those tests.

# Discord Notifications

Maintained official provider for owner-specific Discord webhooks, consuming the
host's Plugin API 1.1.2 protected provider contract. This is a new identity,
`official.discord-notifications`; legacy example credentials/consent are never moved.

Install the package and grant `notification_providers.register` and
`notification_providers.deliver`. An administrator must allow existing runtime
Discord egress. Enable the plugin, then open **Account → Notifications → Discord**
in a compatible host to enroll each webhook. Choose notification types and use
**Send test notification**. Configuration belongs to the host, not a plugin page.

Each webhook is PUBLIC. Default release announcements use public facts. Explicit
confirmation on each destination allows its richer followed-media announcement;
that does not promote trust or permit account details, watch history, ratings,
security messages or recovery tokens. Webhook tokens remain host-encrypted and
never enter this plugin's inputs, files or storage. Removing a destination erases
its secret while preserving history. Reinstallation requires new enrollment.

The renderer returns only `title`, `body`, `event_at` and `link` field references.
The host builds a bounded embed, disables mentions, rejects redirects and owns
retries/failure state. Current implementation supports ordinary webhook channels,
not forum thread creation, DMs, attachments, artwork, Critical urgency or raw payloads.
Delivery confirmation uses Discord's `wait=true` option; see the
[official webhook documentation](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/webhook).

Test: `python -m pytest tests/test_discord_notifications.py -q`.
Build: `python tools/build_packages.py` (isolated preview packages).
Actual host/runtime lifecycle acceptance is separate from unit tests. No external
webhook credentials are bundled. This source is initially an explicit catalogue
preview pending paired acceptance and reviewed signed promotion.

Maintained Discord webhook delivery through the generic provider contract (rich delivery needs Plugin API 1.1.14).
Deploy the paired host provider/settings change before installing this release.

## Setup

1. Install the plugin and approve its provider, storage and outbound-network grants.
2. Open the host's notification settings and enable Discord Webhook for your account.
3. Add a destination using the generated configuration form. Enter a label and an
   ordinary Discord text-channel webhook URL. Multiple destinations are supported.
4. Choose notification types and use **Send test notification** to exercise the
   configured credentials through the core dispatcher.

Webhooks remain PUBLIC. Default media announcements contain public release facts.
Each destination revision can separately opt into the richer followed-media
projection; this does not permit account identifiers, watch history, ratings or
security content. Critical urgency is not supported by this provider.

## Configuration and delivery

The plugin declares its fields, destination kind and features; the host renders
them with shared controls. The plugin validates and stores its own webhook tokens
under opaque installation/destination IDs and revisions. Credentials are never
returned to forms, action results, lifecycle records or host notification rows.
Editing retains an omitted saved URL, invalidates pending work and clears previous
media consent. Removal deletes the URL and retains only a revision tombstone.

Only exact HTTPS discord.com/discordapp.com webhook paths are accepted, without
userinfo, alternate ports, query parameters or fragments. The plugin uses its own
bounded network grant and renders only core-approved content with mentions disabled.
Empty successful Discord responses are accepted; rate limits and server/network
failures are retryable, while invalid/revoked webhook responses fail permanently.
Core owns delivery state, leases, retries, preferences and routing checks.

## Rich batches and editable story messages (host Plugin API 1.1.14)

The webhook declares presentation capabilities (`rich_embeds`, edits, up to 8 digest items,
4 images, link actions) and an `edit` action. Canonical deliveries are laid out by
`sdk/discord_embeds.py` within Discord's hard limits: at most 10 embeds and 6,000 characters
per message, 256/4,096 characters for title/description and 25 fields of 256/1,024 characters.
Truncation is deterministic, a cut description always ends with the live story link, mentions
never notify (`allowed_mentions` parses nothing) and only http(s) links survive. Webhooks cannot
carry buttons, so actions are listed as links in the embed.

Messages are created with `?wait=true`; Discord's message id is returned to the host as the opaque
reference. A later story revision edits that message (`PATCH .../messages/{id}`) while the host
decides it is eligible; a deleted message (HTTP 404/403) is reported as `gone` and the host
sends a selective follow-up instead. Webhook messages cannot be replied to, so follow-ups are
standalone. A reference only works with the webhook that created it. The host-owned test message
keeps the minimal payload. Rate limits (429) and 5xx/network errors are retryable; other errors
fail without blocking other providers. Release order: host (Plugin API 1.1.14) first, then this
package.

## Migration and testing

This release requires explicit enrollment. Historical protected webhook secrets
are not transferred to plugin storage, and automatic update is disabled for this
transition. Old packages remain immutable and notification history is retained.

Standalone source and generated-package tests cover field validation, installation
separation, revision races, secret removal, malformed URLs, approved content and
HTTP failure handling. No production Discord credential is required by those tests.

plugins.readme:
# Epic Games Library

Optional personal Epic game imports through **Plugin API 1.1.11**. Requires a host
that implements `games.import`, connection sync actions and personal scheduled
tasks. Older hosts reject this package during compatibility review;
use an earlier Epic release on a host that predates 1.1.11. This plugin uses the existing SDK v1.1.1 wire helper.
The host page/sign-in support is completed by
[host PR40](https://github.com/obsoletelabs/unnamed_tracking_app_2/pull/40).

## Experimental service dependency

Epic does not publish or support an API for third-party library imports, and
this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Epic Games. It does not use
Epic Online Services or Epic Account Services, and Unnamed Tracking App has no
Epic-issued OAuth client. Instead, the plugin signs in the same way the Epic
Games Launcher does: Epic's own sign-in page returns a one-time authorization
code for the launcher's public client, and the plugin exchanges that code for
launcher access/refresh tokens. It then reads the same unofficial account,
library, playtime and catalogue services the launcher uses.

Those services are undocumented and Epic can change, rate-limit or withdraw them
at any time. Treat the integration as experimental: an Epic-side change can stop
sign-in, imports or playtime until a new plugin release adapts to it. Epic
support cannot help with this plugin; report problems to this repository instead
(see [Troubleshooting and support](#troubleshooting-and-support)).

An Epic service failure is not host data loss. Failed sign-ins, refreshes,
inventory pages, playtime or catalogue lookups stop the current step and keep
your saved connection, checkpoint and library. The plugin never deletes games.
Disconnecting removes only this plugin's saved tokens and checkpoint for your
account; imported games, notes, ratings, status and playtime stay in the host.

## Imported fields

Each Epic game is imported with its title and its Epic identity (catalogue
namespace and item ID, scoped to the connected account). When Epic's catalogue
supplies them, the description, developer and publisher are imported too. Total
playtime is imported when Epic's playtime service answers. Catalogue text is
requested in US English. Artwork, release dates, genres/tags, achievements,
prices, DLC/add-ons and install state are not imported. Use the host's metadata
lookup for artwork and other metadata.

## Connect and import

Install this plugin's `.utp` through Settings → Plugins, approve the declared
permissions and enable it. Open Settings → Account → Connections, where **Epic Games**
is listed with its connection status. Choose **Connect** (or **Manage** once
connected) to open the plugin page in a popup. The page is also reachable at its
plugin route, but it no longer adds a sidebar entry.
The popup uses the host's appearance and spacing, with an account summary and
import controls. Expand **Use your regular browser**, then use **Copy sign-in link** to open Epic in your regular browser while leaving the
app open. If clipboard access is unavailable, copy the selected link manually.
Alternatively, use **Sign in on Epic Games**. The action is declared as external navigation, so
the host validates Epic's returned HTTPS destination and opens it in a new tab,
leaving this popup open; the sandboxed plugin does not open a popup itself.
After signing in, Epic shows a page of text. Select all of it, copy it and paste
it into the code field: pasting the whole page connects without another click.
The one-time authorization code, its JSON page, a single copied JSON line or the
redirect URL are all accepted. Hosts that predate new-tab handling, or a browser
that blocks the tab, navigate the host tab instead; then use browser Back and
reopen **Connections → Epic Games**. No popup permission is needed. Your
password stays on Epic's site. The code is cleared immediately after submission
and is never saved in settings.

If Epic later rejects the saved sign-in (for example after a password change),
the popup shows the code field again. **Replace sign-in** does the same at any
time. The existing connection stays until Epic accepts the new code; an
accepted replacement then starts a fresh import checkpoint, and games already
imported stay in your library.

Launcher access/refresh tokens are validated independently from the 32-character
account ID and bounded to 8 KiB. Hosts must support authorization headers larger
than the original 2 KiB limit; older hosts need the companion token-header fix
before an import can use these tokens. Failed replacement sign-ins retain an
existing connection and never show token values in errors.

Positive, finite access-token lifetimes from Epic are accepted, including lifetimes
longer than one day. The plugin schedules refresh at the shorter of that lifetime
and one day, so a longer provider lifetime does not delay local token rotation.
Malformed expiry values retain an existing connection.

Choose **Import games**. Inventory paging, playtime, catalogue lookup and host
imports run as separate bounded steps. **Pause after this step**, closing the
page or a failed request retains the checkpoint. **Resume import** continues it.
**Start new inventory** deliberately replaces the current checkpoint. Disconnect
removes this user's saved tokens/checkpoint and keeps imported games.

The popup follows Steam's host dialog sizing and shared appearance. Disconnected
accounts show sign-in controls; import controls appear after connecting.
On Games, **Sync / import → Sync Epic Games** starts or resumes the same
import flow. The menu does not add a second connection page.

For automatic imports, open **Account → Background tasks → Epic Games autosync**.
Approve the declared `tasks.background` access and enable your own schedule; it
starts off and normally runs daily. Intervals can range from 5 minutes to 1 week.
Each run advances one bounded checkpoint; incomplete work requests the next step
after 60 seconds, even with the page closed. Completion restores your chosen interval.
Disabling autosync stops queued steps. Manual and automatic imports share the same
per-user lease, tokens, checkpoint and preservation rules; another user's schedule
cannot adopt your Epic account or change your library.

Games use namespace + catalogue identity within the connected account. Similar
titles and another Epic account cannot adopt each other's games. Engine assets,
private sandboxes, DLC and digital extras are skipped. Catalogue requests group
up to 25 entries in one namespace; a missing catalogue response retains the batch
for retry. A repeated/invalid cursor, invalid record, incomplete page or safety
limit stops inventory before availability changes.

Successful imports respect the host's field locks, manual status, notes and
ratings. Playtime only increases; absent/unavailable playtime leaves known values
alone. When multiple launcher artifacts share a catalogue identity, the largest
reported artifact total is used to avoid counting duplicate platform entries.
Only a complete valid inventory can mark previously imported games unavailable.

## Troubleshooting and support

Messages come from the plugin and never include token values. Most Epic-side
failures are recovered by waiting and choosing **Resume import**.

| Message or symptom | What it means and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| "Paste the 32-character authorization code, its JSON page or redirect URL." | The pasted text did not contain exactly one code. Choose **Sign in on Epic Games** (or **Copy sign-in link**) again and paste the whole page Epic shows. Each code works once. |
| "Epic rejected this sign-in. Sign in on Epic again and paste a fresh code." | Epic no longer accepts the saved sign-in (for example after a password change), or rejected the pasted code. Choose **Replace sign-in** and paste a fresh code. If this happens during autosync, the schedule turns itself off; re-enable it in **Account → Background tasks** after reconnecting. |
| "Epic returned a different account. Reconnect before importing." | A token refresh answered for another Epic account. Use **Replace sign-in** with the account you intend to import. As above, re-enable autosync afterwards if it turned off. |
| "Epic is busy. Wait a minute, then resume the import." | Epic rate-limited the request. Wait, then **Resume import**. Autosync retries on its own after at least five minutes. |
| "Epic could not be reached or refused the request. Your saved import is retained." | Epic's service was unavailable or answered with an error. Resume later; the checkpoint is kept. |
| "Epic returned an incomplete inventory…", "…invalid inventory paging information", "…repeated an inventory cursor", "…omitted catalogue entries", "…omitted a game title" or "…unreadable game categories" | Epic's reply did not match what the plugin expects. Nothing is marked unavailable from a partial inventory. Resume later; if it persists across days it is probably an Epic-side change, so report it. |
| "Epic playtime was unavailable. Existing playtime was retained." | Games still import; known playtime is not lowered or cleared. A later import fills playtime when Epic answers again. |
| "Another Epic action is running. Wait briefly, then resume." | Two Epic actions for your account overlapped, for example a manual import and autosync. Wait about a minute and resume. |
| "Start a new import for this connected account." | The saved checkpoint belongs to an earlier connection. Choose **Start new inventory**. |
| "Epic's inventory exceeded the safety limit. Availability has not changed." | The library exceeded 10,000 entries or 200 inventory pages. Report it. |
| "The host denied or could not complete this action. Check plugin permissions, then retry." | A host-side refusal, not an Epic failure. In **Settings → Plugins**, check that the plugin is enabled and its permissions are approved. |
| **Local conflicts** count increases | A game you deleted in the app, or one whose identity changed, is left alone instead of being recreated. |

Only a complete, valid inventory marks games that left your Epic library as
unavailable. They are not deleted, and they become available again when a later
import lists them.

Report persistent Epic sign-in or import failures as an
[issue in this repository](https://github.com/obsoletelabs/unnamed_tracking_app_plugins/issues),
not to Epic or the host application. Include the plugin version (shown in
**Settings → Plugins**), the host release or image tag you deployed and the exact
message. Never include the authorization code, the text of Epic's sign-in page,
the redirect URL, tokens or your Epic account ID. Installation, permission and Connections-page problems that
are not specific to Epic belong to the host's plugin documentation.

# Epic Games Library

Optional personal Epic game imports through **Plugin API 1.1.3**. Requires
[host PR38](https://github.com/obsoletelabs/unnamed_tracking_app_2/pull/38) or a later
host release implementing `games.import`. Older hosts reject this package during
compatibility review. This plugin uses the existing SDK v1.1.1 wire helper.
The host page/sign-in support is completed by
[host PR40](https://github.com/obsoletelabs/unnamed_tracking_app_2/pull/40).

## Connect and import

Install this plugin's `.utp` through Settings → Plugins, approve the declared
permissions and enable it. Open **Epic Games** in the sidebar or its plugin page.
Use **Sign in on Epic Games**, then paste the one-time authorization code, JSON
page or redirect URL into the password field after using browser Back to return.
The host opens the declared Epic sign-in destination outside the sandbox. Your password stays on Epic's site.
The code is cleared immediately after submission and is never saved in settings.

Choose **Import games**. Inventory paging, playtime, catalogue lookup and host
imports run as separate bounded steps. **Pause after this step**, closing the
page or a failed request retains the checkpoint. **Resume import** continues it.
**Start new inventory** deliberately replaces the current checkpoint. Disconnect
removes this user's saved tokens/checkpoint and keeps imported games.

Games use namespace + catalogue identity within the connected account. Similar
titles and another Epic account cannot adopt each other's games. Engine assets,
private sandboxes, DLC and digital extras are skipped. Catalogue requests group
up to 25 entries in one namespace; a missing catalogue response retains the batch
for retry. A repeated/invalid cursor, invalid record, incomplete page or safety
limit stops inventory before availability changes.

Successful imports respect the host's field locks, manual status, notes and
ratings. Playtime only increases; absent/unavailable playtime leaves known values
alone. When multiple launcher artifacts share a catalogue identity, the largest
reported artifact total is used to avoid counting duplicate platform entries.
Only a complete valid inventory can mark previously imported games unavailable.
No game is deleted. Trash or changed local identities are reported as conflicts.

Catalogue artwork and achievements are outside this import. Artwork can be
enriched through the host's existing game metadata tools. This initial plugin
has no automatic background sync, launching or Epic achievement conversion.

## Permissions and credentials

- `games.write`: current-user imports and availability/progress updates.
- `network.outbound`: mediated requests to fixed Epic HTTPS account/library/catalogue services.
- `plugin.storage`: private per-user rotating tokens, account-scoped known identities,
  short atomic leases and resumable checkpoints (16 MiB quota).
- `frontend.navigation.main`: an Epic Games sidebar page. Its packaged frontend
  runs in the host's sandbox and uses the existing appearance/action bridge.

Every operation derives the user from the trusted action context. No supplied
user/account/game ID selects another user's credentials or host records. A
per-user atomic lease serializes token rotation and import checkpoints; after
an interrupted worker the lease expires in 75 seconds. The replacement refresh
token is persisted before inventory/import work. Tokens and remote error bodies
are never returned in UI responses or logged by this plugin.

Private plugin storage uses the runtime's filesystem permissions and isolation;
it is **not encrypted at rest**. Protect the host data directory and backups.
Disconnect forgets this deployment's sign-in; use Epic account security to revoke
sessions on Epic itself when needed.

Epic's launcher library services are not a supported public player-library API
and can change. This implements the legacy import's launcher protocol through
the public gateway. Protocol references: [Epic authentication documentation](https://dev.epicgames.com/docs/web-api-ref/authentication)
and [Legendary's launcher client](https://github.com/legendary-gl/legendary/blob/master/legendary/api/egs.py).
The bundled launcher client ID/credential identifies the public launcher, not
any player's account. No Legendary source is copied or imported.

## Build, tests and distribution

From the plugin repository root:

```sh
python -m pytest tests/test_epic_games.py -q
python tools/check_source_layout.py
python tools/build_packages.py
python tools/distribution.py --root .validation --check-source --include-unreleased
python -m pytest
python -m mkdocs build --strict
```

Branch CI provides an **unsigned-dist** preview for review through the host's
explicit unsigned-install consent. Signed main publication uses the existing
protected official signing pipeline and immutable release history; no private
keys or regenerated historical artifacts belong in this change.

Provider DTO/failure tests use fixtures. Successful live-account import still
requires a user signing in through Epic and checking their own library. Package
installation/runtime/database validation and browser evidence are recorded
separately in the PR; fixtures alone do not certify live Epic availability.

Epic does not publish or support an API for third-party library imports, and
this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Epic Games. It does not use
Epic Online Services or Epic Account Services, and Unnamed Tracking App has no
Epic-issued OAuth client. Instead, the plugin signs in the same way the Epic
Games Launcher does: Epic's own sign-in page returns a one-time authorization
code for the launcher's public client, and the plugin exchanges that code for
launcher access/refresh tokens. It then reads the same unofficial account,
library, playtime and catalogue services the launcher uses.

Those services are undocumented and Epic can change, rate-limit or withdraw them
at any time. Treat the integration as experimental: an Epic-side change can stop
sign-in, imports or playtime until a new plugin release adapts to it. Epic
support cannot help with this plugin; report problems to this repository instead
(see [Troubleshooting and support](#troubleshooting-and-support)).

inventory pages, playtime or catalogue lookups stop the current step and keep
your saved connection, checkpoint and library. The plugin never deletes games.

failures are recovered by waiting and choosing **Resume import**.

| Message or symptom | What it means and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| "Paste the 32-character authorization code, its JSON page or redirect URL." | The pasted text did not contain exactly one code. Choose **Sign in on Epic Games** (or **Copy sign-in link**) again and paste the whole page Epic shows. Each code works once. |
| "Epic rejected this sign-in. Sign in on Epic again and paste a fresh code." | Epic no longer accepts the saved sign-in (for example after a password change), or rejected the pasted code. unavailable. They are not deleted, and they become available again when a later
import lists them.

[issue in this repository](https://github.com/obsoletelabs/unnamed_tracking_app_plugins/issues),
not to Epic or the host application. Include the plugin version (shown in
**Settings → Plugins**), the host release or image tag you deployed and the exact
message. Never include the authorization code, the text of Epic's sign-in page,
the redirect URL, tokens or your Epic account ID. Installation, permission and Connections-page problems that
are not specific to Epic belong to the host's plugin documentation.

# Jellyfin Media Sync â€” official preview

This official preview is under test, with automatic package updates disabled.
The independently installable `official.jellyfin-media-sync` package is
separate from `example.jellyfin-media-sync`, which remains a demonstration.
There is no automatic conversion of the demo's private storage or permission grants.

An administrator adds servers and discovery keys on **Jellyfin servers** directly
under **Administration → Server management** in Settings, tests them, and approves
libraries. Personal connections live at **Account → Your Jellyfin accounts** and
the direct **Media → Jellyfin** sidebar entry. These placements require separate
consent for the administration and account settings areas. Loading and failed
configuration requests show a retry control and the host's access/runtime details;
administrator denial is shown only after a successful role check.
Music, books, Live TV and collections
are excluded. Explicit film/TV/anime mappings win over automatic anime tag/genre
detection. Anime films become a one-episode anime entry; season zero is supported.

On **Jellyfin**, each user connects multiple accounts using a password or Quick
Connect. A password is used once, never persisted. Alternatively, the administrator
can approve a specific remote identity for the shared discovery key. Users can narrow
approved libraries, choose automatic sync and merging, opt into error notifications,
and order accounts for Watch Now. All enabled accounts participate in sync.
Removing a credential retains configuration, item mappings and checkpoints.
Unnumbered episodes retain provider progress and enter review. Assign their real
season/episode numbers or leave them unnumbered; the plugin never fabricates numbers
or marks a partially numbered series complete. Missing runtimes remain unknown.

Sync imports all supported items, including unwatched titles, watched episodes,
position ticks, percentage, play counts and last-played timestamps. Provider IDs
and unique exact title/year matches merge into the user's existing media records.
Ambiguous matches and local watch-state changes enter a review queue. Notes,
ratings and manually locked metadata survive enrichment. Personal ratings are
imported only where absent. Jellyfin supplies descriptions, credits, genres,
studios, countries, languages, tags, dates, codec details, provider identities and
token-free artwork URLs. Year-only dates retain their precision in provider metadata.
Authenticated-only artwork may not display; tokens are never added to image URLs.

Optional **Playback Reporting** imports real individual viewing sessions through
that Jellyfin plugin's read-only user/day API. It requires an installed, active
Playback Reporting plugin and an elevated discovery credential. Choose a bounded
initial lookback (default 30 days, up to 3650). Without it, ordinary Jellyfin cannot
reconstruct earlier sessions from its aggregate counters; the plugin reports this
limitation and never invents past plays or timestamps. No new Jellyfin-side plugin
is required. Sync never changes Jellyfin watched state, ratings, files or media.

One supervised worker processes bounded pages and saves accepted checkpoints.
Host downtime, permission denial and restarts preserve progress. Backoff is bounded
and configurable; authentication/configuration failures wait for correction.
The next automatic run replaces the previous retry schedule, with no overlapping
per-account jobs. Disabling automatic sync stops future schedules; an active run
finishes. Full rescan starts a fresh census. Two successful censuses must miss an
item before its Watch Now link becomes unavailable; personal media is retained.

HTTP and untrusted certificates produce connection-test warnings. HTTPS always
uses host CA trust; there is no certificate-verification bypass. Base URLs may
include a reverse-proxy path; redirects are refused. Secrets stay in private
`plugin.storage` broker namespaces and are never returned by configuration/status
actions. This storage is access-controlled by the runtime, not an encrypted vault;
protect runtime backups accordingly. The plugin has no host database, filesystem,
environment or secret access. Native UI keeps the existing privileged permission
and requires normal user grants. Optional notification denial does not stop sync. With the opt-in, each account has one
notification story (Plugin API 1.1.14): a sync problem opens it, a different problem revises it and a
successful sync resolves it, with a link to the accounts page; hosts or grants without story support
receive the earlier single message.

Target: the current `plugin-manager` public API and Jellyfin 12.1.0. Manifest ranges
remain `^1.0.0`; compatibility detection is intentionally deferred. Provider-neutral
media enrichment and bounded JSON POST are host API additions, available equally
to all plugins. No plugin-specific host hook or trust bypass is used.

Build a validated preview with `python tools/build_packages.py`. Packages and
catalogue previews land under `.validation/`; published historical packages remain
immutable. The 0.0.1 preview is published through the reviewed official signing
identity; automatic updates remain disabled during validation. Unsigned local packages must
use the host's normal untrusted-package approval flow. Test signing keys are for
disposable integration tests only and never confer production trust.

# Jellyfin Media Sync â€” official preview

This official preview is under test, with automatic package updates disabled.
The independently installable `official.jellyfin-media-sync` package is
separate from `example.jellyfin-media-sync`, which remains a demonstration.
There is no automatic conversion of the demo's private storage or permission grants.

An administrator adds servers and discovery keys on **Jellyfin servers** directly
under **Administration → Server management** in Settings, tests them, and approves
libraries. Personal connections live at **Account → Your Jellyfin accounts** and
the direct **Media → Jellyfin** sidebar entry. These placements require separate
consent for the administration and account settings areas. Loading and failed
configuration requests show a retry control and the host's access/runtime details;
administrator denial is shown only after a successful role check.
Music, books, Live TV and collections
are excluded. Explicit film/TV/anime mappings win over automatic anime tag/genre
detection. Anime films become a one-episode anime entry; season zero is supported.

On **Jellyfin**, each user connects multiple accounts using a password or Quick
Connect. A password is used once, never persisted. Alternatively, the administrator
can approve a specific remote identity for the shared discovery key. Users can narrow
approved libraries, choose automatic sync and merging, opt into error notifications,
and order accounts for Watch Now. All enabled accounts participate in sync.
Removing a credential retains configuration, item mappings and checkpoints.
Unnumbered episodes retain provider progress and enter review. Assign their real
season/episode numbers or leave them unnumbered; the plugin never fabricates numbers
or marks a partially numbered series complete. Missing runtimes remain unknown.

Sync imports all supported items, including unwatched titles, watched episodes,
position ticks, percentage, play counts and last-played timestamps. Provider IDs
and unique exact title/year matches merge into the user's existing media records.
Ambiguous matches and local watch-state changes enter a review queue. Notes,
ratings and manually locked metadata survive enrichment. Personal ratings are
imported only where absent. Jellyfin supplies descriptions, credits, genres,
studios, countries, languages, tags, dates, codec details, provider identities and
token-free artwork URLs. Year-only dates retain their precision in provider metadata.
Authenticated-only artwork may not display; tokens are never added to image URLs.

Optional **Playback Reporting** imports real individual viewing sessions through
that Jellyfin plugin's read-only user/day API. It requires an installed, active
Playback Reporting plugin and an elevated discovery credential. Choose a bounded
initial lookback (default 30 days, up to 3650). Without it, ordinary Jellyfin cannot
reconstruct earlier sessions from its aggregate counters; the plugin reports this
limitation and never invents past plays or timestamps. No new Jellyfin-side plugin
is required. Sync never changes Jellyfin watched state, ratings, files or media.

One supervised worker processes bounded pages and saves accepted checkpoints.
Host downtime, permission denial and restarts preserve progress. Backoff is bounded
and configurable; authentication/configuration failures wait for correction.
The next automatic run replaces the previous retry schedule, with no overlapping
per-account jobs. Disabling automatic sync stops future schedules; an active run
finishes. Full rescan starts a fresh census. Two successful censuses must miss an
item before its Watch Now link becomes unavailable; personal media is retained.

HTTP and untrusted certificates produce connection-test warnings. HTTPS always
uses host CA trust; there is no certificate-verification bypass. Base URLs may
include a reverse-proxy path; redirects are refused. Secrets stay in private
`plugin.storage` broker namespaces and are never returned by configuration/status
actions. This storage is access-controlled by the runtime, not an encrypted vault;
protect runtime backups accordingly. The plugin has no host database, filesystem,
environment or secret access. Native UI keeps the existing privileged permission
and requires normal user grants. Optional notification denial does not stop sync.

Target: the current `plugin-manager` public API and Jellyfin 12.1.0. Manifest ranges
remain `^1.0.0`; compatibility detection is intentionally deferred. Provider-neutral
media enrichment and bounded JSON POST are host API additions, available equally
to all plugins. No plugin-specific host hook or trust bypass is used.

Build a validated preview with `python tools/build_packages.py`. Packages and
catalogue previews land under `.validation/`; published historical packages remain
immutable. The 0.0.1 preview is published through the reviewed official signing
identity; automatic updates remain disabled during validation. Unsigned local packages must
use the host's normal untrusted-package approval flow. Test signing keys are for
disposable integration tests only and never confer production trust.

# Jellyfin Media Sync â€” official preview

This official preview is under test, with automatic package updates disabled.
The independently installable `official.jellyfin-media-sync` package is
separate from `example.jellyfin-media-sync`, which remains a demonstration.
There is no automatic conversion of the demo's private storage or permission grants.

An administrator adds servers and discovery keys on **Jellyfin servers** directly
under **Administration → Server management** in Settings, tests them, and approves
libraries. Personal connections live at **Account → Your Jellyfin accounts** and
the direct **Media → Jellyfin** sidebar entry. These placements require separate
consent for the administration and account settings areas. Loading and failed
configuration requests show a retry control and the host's access/runtime details;
administrator denial is shown only after a successful role check.
Music, books, Live TV and collections
are excluded. Explicit film/TV/anime mappings win over automatic anime tag/genre
detection. Anime films become a one-episode anime entry; season zero is supported.

On **Jellyfin**, each user connects multiple accounts using a password or Quick
Connect. A password is used once, never persisted. Alternatively, the administrator
can approve a specific remote identity for the shared discovery key. Users can narrow
approved libraries, choose automatic sync and merging, opt into error notifications,
and order accounts for Watch Now. All enabled accounts participate in sync.
Removing a credential retains configuration, item mappings and checkpoints.
Unnumbered episodes retain provider progress and enter review. Assign their real
season/episode numbers or leave them unnumbered; the plugin never fabricates numbers
or marks a partially numbered series complete. Missing runtimes remain unknown.

Sync imports all supported items, including unwatched titles, watched episodes,
position ticks, percentage, play counts and last-played timestamps. Provider IDs
and unique exact title/year matches merge into the user's existing media records.
Ambiguous matches and local watch-state changes enter a review queue. Notes,
ratings and manually locked metadata survive enrichment. Personal ratings are
imported only where absent. Jellyfin supplies descriptions, credits, genres,
studios, countries, languages, tags, dates, codec details, provider identities and
token-free artwork URLs. Year-only dates retain their precision in provider metadata.
Authenticated-only artwork may not display; tokens are never added to image URLs.

Optional **Playback Reporting** imports real individual viewing sessions through
that Jellyfin plugin's read-only user/day API. It requires an installed, active
Playback Reporting plugin and an elevated discovery credential. Choose a bounded
initial lookback (default 30 days, up to 3650). Without it, ordinary Jellyfin cannot
reconstruct earlier sessions from its aggregate counters; the plugin reports this
limitation and never invents past plays or timestamps. No new Jellyfin-side plugin
is required. Sync never changes Jellyfin watched state, ratings, files or media.

One supervised worker processes bounded pages and saves accepted checkpoints.
Host downtime, permission denial and restarts preserve progress. Backoff is bounded
and configurable; authentication/configuration failures wait for correction.
The next automatic run replaces the previous retry schedule, with no overlapping
per-account jobs. Disabling automatic sync stops future schedules; an active run
finishes. Full rescan starts a fresh census. Two successful censuses must miss an
item before its Watch Now link becomes unavailable; personal media is retained.

HTTP and untrusted certificates produce connection-test warnings. HTTPS always
uses host CA trust; there is no certificate-verification bypass. Base URLs may
include a reverse-proxy path; redirects are refused. Secrets stay in private
`plugin.storage` broker namespaces and are never returned by configuration/status
actions. This storage is access-controlled by the runtime, not an encrypted vault;
protect runtime backups accordingly. The plugin has no host database, filesystem,
environment or secret access. Native UI keeps the existing privileged permission
and requires normal user grants. Optional notification denial does not stop sync.

Target: the current `plugin-manager` public API and Jellyfin 12.1.0. Manifest ranges
remain `^1.0.0`; compatibility detection is intentionally deferred. Provider-neutral
media enrichment and bounded JSON POST are host API additions, available equally
to all plugins. No plugin-specific host hook or trust bypass is used.

Build a validated preview with `python tools/build_packages.py`. Packages and
catalogue previews land under `.validation/`; published historical packages remain
immutable. The 0.0.1 preview is published through the reviewed official signing
identity; automatic updates remain disabled during validation. Unsigned local packages must
use the host's normal untrusted-package approval flow. Test signing keys are for
disposable integration tests only and never confer production trust.

and order accounts for Watch Now. All enabled accounts participate in sync.
Removing a credential retains configuration, item mappings and checkpoints.
Unnumbered episodes retain provider progress and enter review. Assign their real
season/episode numbers or leave them unnumbered; the plugin never fabricates numbers
or marks a partially numbered series complete. Missing runtimes remain unknown.

Sync imports all supported items, including unwatched titles, watched episodes,
position ticks, percentage, play counts and last-played timestamps. Provider IDs
and unique exact title/year matches merge into the user's existing media records.
Ambiguous matches and local watch-state changes enter a review queue. Notes,
ratings and manually locked metadata survive enrichment. Personal ratings are
imported only where absent. Jellyfin supplies descriptions, credits, genres,
studios, countries, languages, tags, dates, codec details, provider identities and
token-free artwork URLs. Year-only dates retain their precision in provider metadata.
Authenticated-only artwork may not display; tokens are never added to image URLs.

Optional **Playback Reporting** imports real individual viewing sessions through
that Jellyfin plugin's read-only user/day API. It requires an installed, active
Playback Reporting plugin and an elevated discovery credential. Choose a bounded
initial lookback (default 30 days, up to 3650). Without it, ordinary Jellyfin cannot
reconstruct earlier sessions from its aggregate counters; the plugin reports this
limitation and never invents past plays or timestamps. No new Jellyfin-side plugin
is required. Sync never changes Jellyfin watched state, ratings, files or media.

One supervised worker processes bounded pages and saves accepted checkpoints.
Host downtime, permission denial and restarts preserve progress. Backoff is bounded
and configurable; authentication/configuration failures wait for correction.
The next automatic run replaces the previous retry schedule, with no overlapping
per-account jobs. Disabling automatic sync stops future schedules; an active run
finishes. Full rescan starts a fresh census. Two successful censuses must miss an
item before its Watch Now link becomes unavailable; personal media is retained.

HTTP and untrusted certificates produce connection-test warnings. HTTPS always
uses host CA trust; there is no certificate-verification bypass. Base URLs may
include a reverse-proxy path; redirects are refused. Secrets stay in private
`plugin.storage` broker namespaces and are never returned by configuration/status
actions. This storage is access-controlled by the runtime, not an encrypted vault;
protect runtime backups accordingly. The plugin has no host database, filesystem,
environment or secret access. Native UI keeps the existing privileged permission
and requires normal user grants. Optional notification denial does not stop sync.

Target: the current `plugin-manager` public API and Jellyfin 12.1.0. Manifest ranges
remain `^1.0.0`; compatibility detection is intentionally deferred. Provider-neutral
media enrichment and bounded JSON POST are host API additions, available equally
to all plugins. No plugin-specific host hook or trust bypass is used.

catalogue previews land under `.validation/`; published historical packages remain
immutable. The 0.0.1 preview is published through the reviewed official signing
identity; automatic updates remain disabled during validation. Unsigned local packages must
use the host's normal untrusted-package approval flow. Test signing keys are for
disposable integration tests only and never confer production trust.

# GiantBomb Metadata Provider

Uses public Plugin API v1.1.1. Install its .utp through Plugin Manager and grant the declared permissions. Configure credentials in the host-rendered provider settings, selecting the plugin-declared system or personal scope. Secrets are write-only and encrypted by the host.

Search returns lightweight identities. Metadata is requested separately for the current top three. Interactive operations are bounded without retries; background operations may pace and retry within their separate budget. Missing credentials, invalid credentials, rate limits and outages return typed failures.

Build development packages with `python tools/build_packages.py`. Unsigned previews require explicit installation consent; the existing release workflow produces signed publication packages.

plugins.readme:
# HowLongToBeat Metadata Provider

The updated source requires public Plugin API **1.1.13** and the host completion-estimates
update in [host PR #136](https://github.com/obsoletelabs/unnamed_tracking_app_2/pull/136).
It uses no account or API key. Install the corresponding published `.utp` through
Plugin Manager and grant its declared metadata, network and storage permissions.

The provider initializes a short-lived public search token, then searches the
site's current endpoint with browser headers. A search 403 renews the token and
retries once; a second rejection stops. Tokens are not persisted or logged. The
SDK returns 403 directly to the provider instead of multiplying that renewal with
generic background retries. Other failures retain bounded SDK pacing/retry policy.

Metadata returns whichever of Main story, Main + extras, Completionist and All
play styles are available, normalized to one-decimal hours. Missing or invalid
figures are omitted, including when Main story is absent. Existing HLTB identity
wins; without one, only a unique exact normalized title is accepted. Community
estimates never write personal playtime. The host applies manual field protection,
account/provider choices and per-category native IGDB fallback independently.

Build development packages with `python tools/build_packages.py`. Unsigned previews require explicit installation consent; the existing release workflow produces signed publication packages.

Run `python -m pytest tests/test_hltb.py tests/test_metadata_providers.py -q`.
Fixtures cover token renewal bounds, partial/invalid figures, selected identity,
ambiguity and the exported wire schema. A direct public token/search check on
15 October 2026 returned five Portal results; this does not establish installed
package success. Package/runtime integration validation is tracked in the PR.

plugins.readme:
# MyAnimeList Metadata Provider

Uses public Plugin API v1.1.1. Install its .utp through Plugin Manager and grant its declared permissions. Jikan's public API needs no credentials, so the provider declares no configuration.

Search returns identities independently of metadata and artwork. Metadata is requested for the current top three; artwork starts after selection. Background refresh uses the same metadata contract for episodes and airing with its own bounded retry policy.

Build unsigned previews with `python tools/build_packages.py`. Preview installation requires explicit consent; signed releases use the existing publication workflow.

Uses public Plugin API v1.1.1. Install its .utp through Plugin Manager and grant its declared permissions. Credentials are configured in the host-rendered provider settings and use the declared system or personal scope. Saved secrets stay hidden.

Search returns identities independently of metadata and artwork. Metadata is requested for the current top three; artwork starts after selection. Background refresh uses the same metadata contract for episodes, airing and relationships with its own bounded retry policy.

Build unsigned previews with `python tools/build_packages.py`. Preview installation requires explicit consent; signed releases use the existing publication workflow.

plugins.readme:
# Password Reset

Maintained optional password recovery integration for host Plugin API 1.1.11. This is a functional account flow; the synthetic example remains a separate demonstration.

## Setup

Install the signed official package and explicitly grant the critical **auth.password_reset** permission globally. Open **Administration → Password policy** and find Password recovery below the policy controls. Choose expiry in minutes or hours (10–60 minutes, default 20). **Save settings**, **Enable** and **Disable** are separate controls. Saving disabled settings does not enable recovery; disabling preserves the saved lifetime and invalidates outstanding links. Installation alone does not enable public recovery. The sign-in request and completion flow is unchanged.

Each user must configure an external notification destination, verify it and separately enable recovery delivery. SMTP is built into the host. A plugin destination must declare verification/security/recovery support and hold the independent high-risk provider grant. The authenticated inbox and browser push cannot carry recovery links. Normal routing preferences and administrator restrictions apply; there is no direct SMTP bypass.

## Use

The sign-in page shows **Forgot your password?** when this contribution is active. Request with your app username or configured app email. The acknowledgement is the same for unknown, disabled, SSO and ineligible accounts. Open the delivered link, choose a password satisfying the server policy and confirm. All browser sessions are revoked; **API keys remain active**. Sign in normally afterward.

Links expire, are single-use and are bound to the current account/password/email, installation and configuration revision. Opening a link never consumes it. Bearer material uses a URL fragment and is removed from the displayed address. Disabling/uninstalling or withdrawing the grant blocks pending delivery/redemption; reinstall cannot reclaim old links.

The host stores encrypted delivery material only until consumption/expiry and never puts it in inbox content or lifecycle audit. This plugin stores only its activation/lifetime configuration and never receives reset tokens, passwords, SMTP credentials or account rows.

## Testing

Run `pytest tests/test_official_password_reset.py` and the paired host recovery suite. Actual signed-package installation and the host request/link/redemption workflow are required before release. Temporary SMTP capture is suitable for local acceptance; no production SMTP account is required.

Startup uses auth_flows.password_reset.restore to resume only an already-active matching installation and definition. Withdrawal or reinstallation requires explicit activation; regranting permission cannot revive an old reset credential.

Configuration is under Settings → Administration → Account security → Password recovery. The page shows live **Account recovery enabled/disabled** from the host. Saved preferences do not imply availability. Requires API1.1.10 and explicit settings placement grants. All SMTP mail now uses the host shared HTML design with a plain alternative.
plugins.release_notes: Password recovery settings now appear on Password policy with separate save, enable and disable controls and readable expiry units. Requires host API1.1.11. Existing sign-in recovery, secure routing, single-use links and session revocation remain unchanged.

plugins.readme:
# Unnamed Tracking PWA

The maintained official PWA integrates the existing mobile repository's PWA
assets with the complete Unnamed Tracking web application. Initial version:
**0.0.1**. The current v1.1 preview uses plugin release **0.0.4**
with reviewed mobile assets at **0.0.4**. Stable 1.0.0 requires an
explicit human release decision.

Install its `.utp` through Plugin Manager, review `frontend.pwa`, and enable it.
The permission publishes public install metadata and icons and enables the
host-owned root worker. It grants no account APIs, native JavaScript or arbitrary
host routes. Only one PWA provider may be enabled per server. The host refuses
conflicting providers rather than selecting one silently.

Use HTTPS (localhost works for development). Android Chrome and Windows
Chrome/Edge offer an install button when available. On iOS Safari, use Share →
Add to Home Screen. Installation requires browser support and is separate from
installing the server plugin. Native Android, WebView and Windows/WinUI clients
remain independent and unchanged.

The installed app opens the full website and uses its normal login/session/SSO.
Passwords are never saved by this plugin. Session expiry returns to normal login.
Offline navigation displays a neutral waiting-for-internet page, never account
data. No `/api/` response is cached. Reconnect restores normal navigation.

The full application, sign-in/SSO redirects and neutral offline page follow
Light, Dark or System and the last device palette, including Orange, Green and
custom colors. Only cosmetic color roles are cached locally; saved account
preferences take precedence online. Browser bars follow the current background.
The public signed installation manifest never contains personal appearance data.

Updates replace the host worker generation and remove only owned old caches.
The offline page has no time expiry. Disable, permission revocation or uninstall
withdraws the manifest/icons and retires the worker when the browser next reaches
the server. Offline devices cannot learn about a server-side removal immediately.
An installed shortcut remains an ordinary website shortcut, with plugin settings
guidance. Reinstallation gets a new installation/cache identity.

Assets are synchronized from `unnamed-tracking-mobile-app/pwa` using
`tools/sync_pwa.py --mobile-root PATH --host-root PATH`; `--check` validates exact
provenance and a plugin release that does not precede its mobile asset version.
The host never executes a worker from an
untrusted package: reviewed worker/offline infrastructure is shipped by the host.
Metadata colors are typed for future theme support; no mobile UI redesign is
included.

Development previews may be unsigned and require explicit untrusted-package
consent. They do not receive the verified Official badge. Official publication
requires a separately registered official public key and protected signing secret.
See [signing configuration](../../docs/official-signing.md).

# Unnamed Tracking PWA

The maintained official PWA integrates the existing mobile repository's PWA
assets with the complete Unnamed Tracking web application. Initial version:
**0.0.1**. The current v1.1 preview uses plugin release **0.0.4**
with reviewed mobile assets at **0.0.4**. Stable 1.0.0 requires an
explicit human release decision.

Install its `.utp` through Plugin Manager, review `frontend.pwa`, and enable it.
The permission publishes public install metadata and icons and enables the
host-owned root worker. It grants no account APIs, native JavaScript or arbitrary
host routes. Only one PWA provider may be enabled per server. The host refuses
conflicting providers rather than selecting one silently.

Use HTTPS (localhost works for development). Android Chrome and Windows
Chrome/Edge offer an install button when available. On iOS Safari, use Share →
Add to Home Screen. Installation requires browser support and is separate from
installing the server plugin. Native Android, WebView and Windows/WinUI clients
remain independent and unchanged.

The installed app opens the full website and uses its normal login/session/SSO.
Passwords are never saved by this plugin. Session expiry returns to normal login.
Offline navigation displays a neutral waiting-for-internet page, never account
data. No `/api/` response is cached. Reconnect restores normal navigation.

The full application, sign-in/SSO redirects and neutral offline page follow
Light, Dark or System and the last device palette, including Orange, Green and
custom colors. Only cosmetic color roles are cached locally; saved account
preferences take precedence online. Browser bars follow the current background.
The public signed installation manifest never contains personal appearance data.

Updates replace the host worker generation and remove only owned old caches.
The offline page has no time expiry. Disable, permission revocation or uninstall
withdraws the manifest/icons and retires the worker when the browser next reaches
the server. Offline devices cannot learn about a server-side removal immediately.
An installed shortcut remains an ordinary website shortcut, with plugin settings
guidance. Reinstallation gets a new installation/cache identity.

Assets are synchronized from `unnamed-tracking-mobile-app/pwa` using
`tools/sync_pwa.py --mobile-root PATH --host-root PATH`; `--check` validates exact
provenance and a plugin release that does not precede its mobile asset version.
The host never executes a worker from an
untrusted package: reviewed worker/offline infrastructure is shipped by the host.
Metadata colors are typed for future theme support; no mobile UI redesign is
included.

consent. They do not receive the verified Official badge. Official publication
requires a separately registered official public key and protected signing secret.

plugins.readme:
# User Invites

Maintained official administrator email-invite integration for host Plugin API **1.1.11**.

Configure built-in SMTP in Administration > Notifications. Install this plugin and explicitly approve `auth.user_invites`. Open Administration > Users: User invitations appears below the user controls, and Invite user sits beside Create user. Save settings separately from enabling or disabling invitations. Choose expiry using minutes, hours, days or weeks, within the existing one-hour to one-week bounds (one day by default). Send to the intended recipient email address; do not create an account first.

Email settings include a From display name, subject, heading, welcome message, personal/generic/no greeting, button wording, card/simple layout, accent color and footer. The optional recipient name supplies the personal greeting. A live preview shows the wording and appearance. All content is plain text and escaped by the host. The configured SMTP sender address and host acceptance URL remain authoritative. Wording changes affect future invitations and preserve existing links; lifetime changes and disabling retain credential invalidation behavior. Disabling preserves saved settings. Installation alone does not enable invitations.

The host queues a PRIVATE bootstrap email through the existing notification dispatcher. It uses the configured public app URL, falling back to the issuing administrator's signed-in app address. An allowed secure SMTP transport is required; explicit local-IP/development plaintext exceptions follow the built-in policy. Routing restrictions still apply. The destination exists only for that invitation and cannot receive ordinary or security notices.

The invitee opens the emailed link and chooses a username/password. Opening the link does not consume it. POST acceptance creates an active normal account, never an administrator, and requires normal sign-in afterward. The email address cannot be changed by the acceptance payload. Possession of the invite does not create a verified notification destination automatically.

The administrator page lists the current installation's last 100 invites, expiry and delivery state, and can revoke outstanding links. Sending another invite to the same address retires the earlier link. Requests are bounded to 100 per administrator/day and five per recipient/day, with a global 1,000-row pending capacity. Expired pre-account records are cleaned after a day. Disabling, uninstalling or revoking the grant invalidates old links; reinstall requires explicit activation.

The plugin owns activation and its admin UI. It uses only the public gateway and receives its own invitation email/status records. The host owns tokens, account/password validation, creation, SMTP credentials and delivery retries. Passwords and bearer links never pass through plugin code. Existing registered emails are rejected to the administrator.

This is a usable flow, separate from the synthetic `example.user-invite-notification-demo` routing demonstration.

Configure activation/lifetime under Settings → Administration → Account security → User invitations. On Administration → Users, **Invite user** opens the plugin dialog to send and review invitations. Requires API1.1.10 and reviewed administrative/settings grants. The host renders invitation mail as HTML plus text.
plugins.release_notes: Integrated Users-page settings and Invite user button beside Create user. Separate save/enable/disable controls, expiry units and customizable email wording, sender display name, greeting and appearance. Requires host API1.1.11; the host retains SMTP, credential and account ownership.
